After three minutes of a task that encouraged head movement, spatial accuracy declined by 0.59 cm, while the gaze center at each target shifted by a mean distance of only 0.37 cm. On the validation block, the offset was 0.30 cm larger for men than for women. Age, region of residence, face luminance, and Michelson contrast showed no reliable relationship with spatial accuracy. A higher eye aspect ratio, a more open eye, was associated with a smaller offset. Wearing glasses decreased spatial accuracy on every validation block. In a comparison between a random subsample ($N = 101$) and a separate sample tested with the open-source tracker WebGazer ($N = 101$) using an identical protocol, Chiasm showed better spatial accuracy (2.18 vs. 4.51 cm) and spatial precision (SD; 1.01 vs. 1.55 cm). WebGazer showed better sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S; 0.79 vs. 1.26 cm), which likely reflects conservative, over-smoothed estimates rather than superior stability. These results suggest that Chiasm is narrowing the gap between webcam and hardware-based eye tracking, making large-scale gaze research "in the wild" a reality.

items.title_en: Learning Where to Look: Observation Policy Optimization for Thinking with Images
items.abstract_en: Complex visual question answering often requires vision-language models to think with images, i.e., actively acquire local visual evidence by zooming into informative regions of high-resolution images. Our error analysis shows that many failures in this setting originate from incorrect observation actions, where the model fails to localize key regions or obtain crops that contain sufficient evidence for answering. We further observe that bounding-box tokens exhibit substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens, indicating high uncertainty when the model decides where to look. However, existing reinforcement learning methods based on final-answer rewards provide only trajectory-level feedback, making it difficult to assign precise credit to the observation actions. We propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), an RL algorithm for optimizing observation actions in tool-augmented thinking with images. OPO consists of two core modules. First, Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching (UOB) treats each image zoom-in tool call as an observation event and selectively branches at high-uncertainty, low-redundancy events during rollout, enabling efficient exploration of alternative cropping decisions and their resulting visual evidence. Second, Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution (ELAA) compares sibling branches using local evidence-sufficiency rewards and assigns credit only to the corresponding observation-action tokens. By decoupling observation-action optimization from trajectory-level outcome supervision, OPO improves visual evidence acquisition and further enhances visual reasoning performance. Experiments show that OPO consistently improves Qwen3-VL models across scales and achieves competitive performance against larger models and tool-augmented baselines. Code is publicly available.

items.title_en: HTNN-MSC: Multi-view Subspace Clustering with a Hyperbolic Tangent Tensor Low-Rank Surrogate
items.abstract_en: High-order dependencies among views can be modeled by tensor singular value decomposition (t-SVD) in multi-view subspace clustering. However, the tensor nuclear norm often used with this framework assigns the same asymptotic marginal penalty to singular values of different magnitudes, which may excessively shrink dominant components that encode cluster structure. We propose HTNN-MSC, which replaces this norm with a bounded hyperbolic tangent tensor rank surrogate. The surrogate is strictly concave on the positive half-axis and has a Lipschitz continuous derivative. Its marginal penalty decreases as singular values grow. We develop an alternating direction method of multipliers solver in which the tensor subproblem decomposes into scalar frequency-domain shrinkage problems. Safeguarded multi-start Newton iterations and candidate-objective comparison implement the resulting hyperbolic tangent thresholding operator. The shape parameter is scaled by the input spectrum. We also establish o-minimal definability of the augmented objective. Under explicit boundedness, descent, relative-error, and exact-block conditions, the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz framework guarantees convergence of the full sequence to a KKT point. On 23 datasets, HTNN-MSC achieves a mean clustering accuracy of 0.8404 and an average accuracy rank of 2.78 against nine representative methods. Friedman tests and Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon comparisons reveal significant overall differences, although several pairwise differences remain nonsignificant. HTNN-MSC records 19 wins, one tie, and three losses against the convex t-SVD-MSC skeleton. A same-skeleton ablation also shows that the proposed surrogate does not uniformly outperform alternative nonconvex penalties.

items.title_en: Robustness Verification against Patch Attacks via Group-Lasso Semidefinite Relaxation
items.abstract_en: Robustness verification is essential for ensuring the safety and security of neural networks, but current methods focus heavily on norm-ball attacks, which do not adequately model typical real-world threats that present physical perturbations, known as patch attacks. A naive approach requires computationally prohibitive enumeration of all possible patch positions. To address the challenge, we propose a novel neural network verification method specialized to the patch-attack threat. Instead of enumerating patch locations, we first model the patch attack with group-wise sparsity and formulate its verification methods as a mixed-integer semidefinite program (MISDP) by applying SDP relaxation to the neural network. We then propose three relaxations, including Group-Lasso relaxation, that remove the integer variables while preserving the sparse, group-wise structure of the original attack, enabling substantially efficient verification. Our empirical analysis demonstrates that the proposed relaxations require less than 3% of the computation time of the original MISDP, while the Group-Lasso relaxation incurs only a 0.34\% average increase in the objective value over the original formulation. Furthermore, Group-Lasso achieves a verified rate of 91%, compared with under 70% for prior methods.

items.title_en: VISTA: Vision-Language Integrated Semantic Triage Architecture for Online Face Clustering in Long Videos
items.abstract_en: Clustering faces by identity in long, continuous video streams is a challenging task that serves as a building block for human-centric video analysis. The majority of existing face clustering models are offline, i.e., they assume the entire data to be available altogether. In many practical scenarios, however, the entire data is either unavailable or poses computational challenges to be processed in its entirety. A handful of online methods that exist rely on geometric visual features and simple thresholding techniques, which fail when the faces exhibit significant appearance variations in long, unconstrained videos. To this end, we present VISTA, the first vision language framework for online face clustering in long videos. VISTA leverages semantic reasoning in a controlled, uncertainty aware fashion to maintain both high cluster purity and long range identity continuity. This makes it robust to the variations in illumination, pose, and costume changes that the faces and characters exhibit in long real world videos. Extensive experiments on the VPCD benchmark dataset (with 15 full episodes from The Big Bang Theory [2007-2019], Buffy the Vampire Slayer [1997-2003], and Sherlock [2010-2017]) demonstrate that VISTA achieves a robust precision and recall balance, consistently improving over the strongest matched online unsupervised baseline (COFC) under identical detector, embeddings, and evaluation protocol. Code and supplementary material: https://github.com/SkyJiashu/VISTA.

items.title_en: EP-LVMQA: Evidence-Preserving Coarse-to-Fine Localization for Low-Quality Long Video Moment Question Answering
items.abstract_en: Long instructional videos are increasingly used in medical education, industrial training, and procedural knowledge transfer, yet their evidence is often incomplete or unreliable: subtitles may be missing, ASR noisy, OCR sparse, and decisive actions briefly shown without narration. Existing VideoQA systems typically return labels or free-form text, making answer support difficult to inspect. We study Long Video Moment Question Answering (LVMQA), where a system returns timestamped answer-supporting evidence. We propose EP-LVMQA, an evidence-preserving coarse-to-fine framework comprising an Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Evidence Timeline, a Coarse Evidence Planner, and an Evidence-Conditioned Fine Localizer. An evidence card transfers planner scores, matched cues, source-confidence proxies, modality-specific evidence, neighboring context, and a temporal prior between the latter two modules. On MedVidQA, EP-LVMQA achieves 26.1 R1@0.5 and 31.8 mIoU, improving the strongest non-ours results by 6.3 and 5.1 points. It raises Suff.@2 and Ver.@2 to 25.4 and 22.6, gains of 9.5 and 8.8 points. Under matched low-quality perturbations, average relative degradation is reduced from the strongest non-ours value of 14.6% to 11.1%. On Ego4D-NLQ and QVHighlights, EP-LVMQA remains broadly comparable to established task-specific localization methods.

items.title_en: MiCaDe: Online LiDAR-Camera Miscalibration Change Detection for Autonomous Driving
items.title_zh: MiCaDe：面向自动驾驶的在线激光雷达-相机失准变化检测
items.abstract_en: Reliable multi-sensor perception in autonomous vehicles requires accurate calibration between cameras and LiDAR. However, calibration drift is often unavoidable in long-term deployments: vibrations, thermal effects, and minor mechanical shocks may alter the relative pose between sensors, leading to systematic errors in downstream fusion tasks. We propose MiCaDe (Miscalibration Change Detection), an online solution detecting when the extrinsic LiDAR-camera calibration parameters are no longer accurate by means of sequential change detection. MiCaDe requires no calibration targets, or modification of the perception stack, providing low false-alarm rates with negligible computational overhead. Our key insight is that 3D and 2D bounding boxes produced by standard object detectors should remain geometrically consistent under correct calibration. By matching cross-modal detections, we derive geometric consistency metrics that serve as sensitive indicators of extrinsic drift. These metrics are aggregated into fixed-size batches and scored against a reference distribution, producing a likelihood stream that is monitored by a Change Point Model (CPM). Crucially, the CPM accumulates statistical evidence over time, enabling detection of subtle drifts that would otherwise go unnoticed. Experiments on multiple long-sequence datasets and on a real-world dataset with physically induced miscalibration confirm reliable detection under diverse conditions. Code available at: https://github.com/CarloSgaravatti/MiCaDe.

items.title_en: Heads That Write, Not Just Point: Image Retrieval Heads in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract_en: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) can process interleaved text and multiple images in a single context, but how they internally identify the image relevant to a question remains poorly understood. We study this grounding step as in-context image retrieval and introduce ICIR-MCQ, a controlled probe for head-level analysis of image retrieval. Using each head's attention mass over image-token spans, we first identify sparse pointer heads that reliably point to the target image. These heads transfer beyond the probe: a single pointer head is competitive with external vision-language retrievers on a naturalistic multi-image retrieval benchmark, showing that LVLMs contain a strong internal image retrieval signal. Attention alone, however, shows where a head reads from, not what its output passes on to later layers, so we introduce a complementary output-side analysis. For each head, we train a lightweight image retriever on its value-weighted output and use it to identify writer heads, whose outputs contain enough information to identify the target image. Surprisingly, the pointer and writer criteria select substantially different head sets, with only 35 to 47 heads overlapping among the top-100 heads under each criterion. Targeted set-partition ablations show that the heads most important for standard multi-image inference are concentrated in this pointer-writer intersection, while heads selected by only one criterion show less consistent separation from random-head controls. The most consistent causal effects arise from heads selected by both the attention-based pointer and output-side writer criteria. Code and data: https://github.com/parkquasar/Image-Retrieval-Heads.

items.title_en: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
items.abstract_en: Multimodal agents use web and image tools to answer questions beyond their internal knowledge. Some search tasks use images mainly to identify an initial entity, then rely on text retrieval. These tasks offer limited insight into how agents connect information across images, objects, and search steps. We therefore focus on visual context management. This involves organizing and using visual information and linking it to other findings during search. Visually intensive tasks require agents to combine object appearance, local details, or spatial relations with external information. We introduce VisSearch-Bench, with 204 human-written tasks across 7 main domains and 25 subdomains. It covers Set-wise Visual Search, Sequential Visual Search, Hybrid Wide-Deep Search, Competitive Visual Disambiguation, and Visual-Structure-Guided Search. Each task provides a reference answer, traceable evidence, and scoring rules. Accuracy measures complete task success, while Process Score measures the correctness and completeness of individual results and subquestion answers. Across 16 multimodal models, the best system fully solves only 26.47% of tasks, even with search tools. These results highlight the challenge of linking visual evidence with search results to produce complete answers.

items.title_en: Influence of Geometry and Tissue Damage on the Mechanical Behaviour of Skin Meshing
items.abstract_en: Skin meshing increases graft coverage, yet the clinically achieved expansion often falls below the manufacturer's nominal meshing ratio. Previous elastic analyses have demonstrated that mesh topology and skin anisotropy strongly influence graft expansion; however, the effect of progressive damage at larger deformation remains unexplored. This study therefore investigates how progressive damage affects the expansion and mechanical response of skin meshes. The performance of auxetic mesh geometries is compared with conventional Zimmer mesher (ZM) geometry. Human back skin was modelled using a one-term Ogden ground matrix and a Gasser Ogden Holzapfel (GOH) collagen network, with separate scalar Kachanov-type continuum damage variables for each constituent. The auxetic geometries, including 1st- and 2nd-order alternative slits (AS1 and AS2), I-shaped (IS) and H-shaped (HS) re-entrant patterns, and ZM, were analysed with Langer's lines oriented either parallel or perpendicular to the loading direction. Hyperelastic and damage-based formulations were compared up to 25% strain, and the damage-based simulations were subsequently extended to 40% strain. ZM was further loaded to 155% strain; the area ratios attained by HS at 40% strain were matched by ZM at 142.1% and 124.7% strain for Langer's lines parallel and perpendicular to loading, respectively. Results indicate that HS achieves greater coverage than ZM for a given stretch, whereas its damage advantage depends on the orientation of Langer's lines.

items.title_en: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: From Specialist Models to Unified Models
items.abstract_en: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is among the oldest and most widely deployed applications of artificial intelligence. This survey reviews its development, focusing on the Foundation Model Era. We define OCR through faithful transcription: within a specified visual scope, OCR should completely reconstruct the text, notation, and document structure observable in the source image, and every textual, notational, or structural element in the output must be verifiable from visual evidence in that image. We trace the development from specialist OCR models toward unified models, examining joint text detection and recognition, structured sequence generation, and the use of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs). We organize contemporary OCR systems into five coexisting families: modular toolkits and task-specific models, specialized document VLMs, hybrid workflows, general-purpose VLMs, and commercial products and managed services. We compare their architectures, data, and training, examining hallucination and omission, insufficient spatial grounding, and inference cost in generative OCR. We review evaluation from character and scene text recognition to parsing individual structural elements and full-page transcription, highlighting gaps in consistent output definitions, attribution of performance to individual components, and coverage of real capture conditions and visible content and structure. Finally, we summarize the challenges facing OCR and discuss directions for future research. We continuously track related work at https://github.com/zhihengli-casia/Awesome-OCR-in-the-Foundation-Model-Era.

items.title_en: Trusting Imagined Futures: Auditing Imagined Rewards for VLA Post-Training
items.abstract_en: Video world models enable candidate actions to be evaluated through imagined outcomes, but high predicted rewards can favor trajectories with poor execution quality. We introduce Trusting Imagined Futures (TIF), an offline supervision selection method for vision-language-action (VLA) post-training that audits predicted rewards using execution feedback. A multidimensional reward model predicts a utility score for candidate ranking and five dimensions of execution quality. An auditor uses reward predictions and uncertainty to identify overestimation patterns learned from paired imagined videos and real executions. TIF accepts the candidate with the highest predicted utility when its advantage over the existing trajectory exceeds a margin and its audit risk passes a threshold; otherwise, it retains the existing supervision. The retained real trajectories then supervise behavior cloning. Across four LIBERO suites and three training seeds, TIF achieves a mean success rate of 76.25%, improving over training on the existing trajectories by 3.00 percentage points with the same trajectory count and training budget. Adding audit gating yields 1.47 percentage points with the reward model and advantage margin held fixed. The gains persist against advantage ranking and logistic regression risk selection at matched replacement counts. On recorded videos from three real robot tasks, TIF increases clean completion among selected trajectories from 58.33% to 70.00% across 60 candidate pools.

items.title_en: Radial distortion homography estimation from affine-covariant or orientation-covariant features
items.abstract_en: We present minimal solvers for joint homography and radial distortion estimation using affine- or orientation-covariant features. The core contribution is a set of novel constraints that exploit local feature geometry inherent to affine descriptors, enabling solvers that require fewer correspondences than point-based methods. Using modern robust estimation frameworks, we demonstrate that the proposed solvers are advantageous to the current state-of-the-art with a significant speed-up in the presence of outliers while maintaining comparable or superior estimation accuracy. The proposed solvers are tested on both synthetic and real images containing challenging fisheye distortions.

items.title_en: NightIQA: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for MLLM-Based Nighttime Image Quality Assessment
items.abstract_en: Nighttime images are inherently susceptible to complex, compound degradations, making accurate quality assessment exceptionally challenging. Score-based IQA methods condense quality into a single number, lacking the multi-dimensional, language-grounded reasoning required for nighttime evaluation. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a more comprehensive alternative, yet remain constrained by a critical data gap: existing real-world IQA datasets are overwhelmingly daytime-centric and often built from outdated captures, while synthetic alternatives lack nighttime-specific degradation modeling, yielding artifacts far removed from authentic nighttime conditions. To bridge this gap, we present NightIQA, a dataset and benchmark suite purpose-built for MLLM-based nighttime IQA. It comprises three core components: NightIQA-Real, a real-world dataset of 1,769 high-resolution images that we captured ourselves with modern equipment, encompassing six canonical distortion types and structured multi-dimensional annotations; NightIQA-Bench, a benchmark of 1,078 visually grounded multiple-choice questions tailored to MLLM-based nighttime IQA, organized around a four-level evaluation hierarchy spanning Perception, Technical Assessment, Localization, and Reasoning; and NightIQA-Syn, an inherently scalable, scene-aware synthesis pipeline that jointly models global-level and instance-level degradations, with an initial release of 80k high-fidelity images alongside the full generation code. Fine-tuned on NightIQA with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), Qwen3-VL-8B outperforms open-source IQA methods and achieves higher overall accuracy than leading closed-source models, highlighting the value of domain-specific data and structured supervision.

items.title_en: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification
items.title_zh: LIPS-PC：学习用于单像素分类的照明模式
items.abstract_en: In single-pixel (ghost) imaging, known illumination patterns probe an object and a detector with no spatial resolution returns one number per pattern. Each measurement costs acquisition time and photons and, for ionizing probes, contributes to delivered dose. Motivated by automated radiographic defect screening, where a class label suffices, we introduce Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification (LIPS-PC). The patterns are learned end-to-end while the measurement operator remains one fixed linear matrix, identical for every input. We parameterize it as a residual correction to a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (2D-DCT), $D=D_{\mathrm{base}}+Δ$, and jointly train the correction and a compact classifier using cross-entropy, without a reconstruction objective. This yields a task-driven linear embedding through optimization. We evaluate LIPS-PC numerically on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST under a controlled protocol, then on RIAWELC, a real industrial X-ray weld-radiograph dataset. Across five budgets, $M\in{8,16,32,64,128}$, corresponding to sampling ratios from below 1% to 12.5%, the learned operator outperforms the best tested fixed transform by 9-15 percentage points at $M=8$ on all three datasets. Its eight-measurement accuracy requires roughly 16-32 measurements with the best fixed transform, indicating a $2\times$ to $4\times$ saving at comparable accuracy. The advantage generally shrinks as $M$ increases, with a small reversal on RIAWELC at higher budgets. These results show that learning what to measure is especially valuable when measurements are scarce.

items.title_en: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception
items.title_zh: iMED：用于手术3D感知的多内窥镜数据集
items.abstract_en: We introduce iMED, the first synchronized multi-endoscope dataset for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery (RAMIS), designed to address a fundamental limitation in surgical vision benchmarking: the absence of independent held-out viewpoints. Existing surgical datasets capture single-trajectory sequences from a single endoscope, making it impossible to distinguish geometric generalization from photometric interpolation along a narrow forward-facing path. iMED provides 340 sequences ~170K synchronized timepoints with 4 views per timepoint) recorded simultaneously from two independent stereo endoscopes across ex vivo, postmortem, and live surgical settings, spanning 14 specimens with diverse anatomical regions and motion regimes. The dataset includes calibrated camera intrinsics, ArUco-based frame-wise pose estimates with uncertainty quantification, instrument segmentation masks, and rich clinical metadata. Using a train-on-one-endoscope, test-on-another evaluation protocol, we benchmark 23 state-of-the-art methods across rigid and deformable novel view synthesis, pose estimation, feature matching, and monocular depth estimation. Our experiments show that methods relying primarily on photometric supervision degrade substantially under this held-out-endoscope setting, while methods with explicit geometric regularization are more robust across views in our benchmark. Notably, large-scale foundation models transfer surprisingly well to surgical imagery, often outperforming domain-specific models, suggesting pitfalls in current fine-tuning protocols. iMED establishes a new evaluation protocol for geometric generalization in surgical vision.

items.title_en: Learning from Unlabeled Photographs for General Oral Image Analysis
items.title_zh: 从无标注照片中学习用于通用口腔图像分析
items.abstract_en: Oral photographs contain rich clinical information and hold significant potential for artificial intelligence applications; however, most models are trained for individual tasks and rely on costly expert annotations. We hypothesized that self-supervised training on unlabeled oral photographs could produce transferable visual representations for heterogeneous vision tasks. To test this hypothesis, we developed DOVE (Dental Optical Visual Encoder) by domain-adaptive self-supervised pretraining on approximately 530,000 unlabeled oral photographs collected from publicly accessible sources. DOVE was benchmarked against 3 established baselines across 5 classification datasets and 4 segmentation datasets, covering both frozen backbone evaluation and end-to-end finetuning. DOVE achieved the strongest overall performance, ranking best in few-shot transfer and label efficiency on most benchmarks. Under the 20-shot frozen-backbone protocol, DOVE outperformed the second best DINOv3 by 4.37 percentage points in mean macro-F1 across classification datasets and by 4.49 percentage points in mean macro-Dice across segmentation tasks. Under end-to-end finetuning, DOVE achieved at least 80% of the strongest full-data baseline's performance across most evaluation datasets using only 10% of the labeled training data. Qualitative retrieval and feature analyses further indicated better organization of image-level and spatial representations. These findings support DOVE as a generalizable and label-efficient backbone for oral vision research.

items.title_en: BhopalMLS: A LiDAR Dataset for Semantic Scene Understanding in Heterogeneous Urban Environments
items.title_zh: BhopalMLS：用于异构城市环境中语义场景理解的LiDAR数据集
items.abstract_en: We introduce BhopalMLS, a large-scale Mobile Laser Scanning (MLS) dataset from a dense, heterogeneous urban environment in Bhopal, India, with mixed traffic, informal structures, and narrow unplanned streets. It spans approximately 10 km of road corridors with over 1.2 billion points and 19,518 annotated instances across 62 fine-grained static categories, grouped into 12-class and 21-class benchmark taxonomies; 6 optional moving-class subclasses support dynamic-object analysis. Existing 3D datasets, collected in well-planned cities, are structurally more uniform than such unplanned settings, and lack their subtype diversity. On semantic and instance segmentation at both granularities, fine-tuned foundation models surpass supervised baselines: Utonia(L) reaches 71.28% mIoU (vs. PTv3's 68.04% from scratch) and 44.07% mAP50 on the 12-class benchmark. Cross-region experiments against four established datasets (Ke-MLS, Toronto-3D, Paris-Lille-3D, SemanticKITTI) reveal a consistent asymmetric transferability: models trained on BhopalMLS transfer better than the reverse on every pair, for both Utonia(L) and Concerto(L) (mean 21.5, up to 36 mIoU points), holding even when the target is denser. Factor-controlled retraining at a fixed label budget, repeated on both models, attributes this to the coverage of BhopalMLS's subtype inventory rather than to dataset size or corridor geometry: collapsing each class to a single subtype costs 13.0 and 13.3 mIoU points for Utonia(L) and Concerto(L). BhopalMLS therefore offers a testbed for 3D perception beyond well-planned cities. Data and an interactive viewer are at https://geoai4cities.github.io/bhopalmls.

items.title_en: Polyp Matching Using Deep Learning
items.title_zh: 使用深度学习的息肉匹配
items.abstract_en: A key challenge in colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) analysis is accurately identifying whether multiple images depict the same polyp, which is critical to avoid over-counting and unnecessary clinical interventions. Additionally, this prevents prolonged follow-up colonoscopies where endoscopists search for duplicate polyps without precise localization. This study presents a novel contrastive learning-based approach to polyp matching using a Siamese neural network architecture. The model was trained on a dataset from the Danish CareForColon2015 trial. The dataset comprises 5,103 image pairs of confirmed same polyp and 5,103 pairs of different polyps, annotated by experienced clinicians. The proposed model employs ResNet variants (ResNet18, ResNet34, ResNet50), DenseNet121 and EfficientNet B0/B3 as backbones and utilizes contrastive learning with cosine vector distance metric for classification. Experimental results demonstrate high classification accuracies of up to 92% and AUC values close to 0.98. These results suggest that automated polyp matching has the potential to reduce polyp over-counting, improve patient risk stratification, and reduce unnecessary follow-up colonoscopies.

items.title_en: Locomotor activity enhances environmental representation by boosting visuo-frontal communication
items.title_zh: 运动活动通过增强视觉—前额叶通讯提升环境表征
items.abstract_en: During environment exploration we rapidly acquire visual information to identify targets of interest. Here, we discovered that locomotion limits how long natural scenes are viewed dur- ing free exploration. Whether the brain has developed compensatory mechanisms to ensure that sensory information is accurately transmitted to downstream areas during and after locomotion is unknown. We examined this issue by recording the spiking activity of popula- tions of neurons in visual and prefrontal cortex in conjunction with wireless recordings of oculomotor events while macaques moved freely to explore their environment or performed treadmill bipedal locomotion. The communication between visuo-frontal cortical areas was enhanced during and after locomotion to increase visual-evoked responses and population coding accuracy in prefrontal, but not visual cortical neurons. This in turn improved behav- ioral performance in a freely moving visual detection task after locomotion. Electrical stim- ulation further revealed elevated inter-areal synaptic efficacy during locomotor activity. The mechanism whereby locomotion enhances stimulus coding accuracy in prefrontal cortex and behavioral performance by increasing visuo-frontal communication is functionally beneficial during environmental exploration when incoming stimuli are rapidly changing and the win- dow for perceptual decisions is temporally restricted.
items.abstract_zh: 在环境探索中，我们能快速获取视觉信息以识别目标。本研究发现，自由探索时运动（locomotion）会限制单个自然场景被观看的时长。大脑是否演化出补偿机制，以确保运动期间及之后感觉信息仍能准确传至下游区域，此前未知。作者在猕猴自由移动探索或进行跑步机双足行走时，同步无线记录眼动事件，并记录视觉皮层与前额叶皮层神经元群体的放电活动。结果显示，运动期间及之后视—额通讯增强，使前额叶（而非视觉皮层）神经元的视觉诱发反应与群体编码准确性提高，进而改善运动后自由移动视觉检测任务的行为表现。电刺激进一步揭示运动时区域间突触效能升高。即运动通过增强视—额通讯提升前额叶刺激编码精度与行为表现；当传入刺激快速变化、知觉决策窗口受限时，该机制在环境探索中具有功能益处。
items.highlight_zh: 运动增强视—额通讯，让大脑在仓促探索中保持编码精度
items.digest_zh:
一、问题：动物在环境中走动探索时，眼睛停在每个场景上的时间会被“走动”本身压缩——看得更仓促，但知觉判断还得准。大脑是否用某种补偿机制，保证运动中和运动后视觉信息仍能准确传到下游（如前额叶），此前并不清楚。
二、方法：研究者在猕猴自由走动探索、或在跑步机上双足行走时，用无线设备同步记录眼动事件，同时用多电极记录视觉皮层与前额叶皮层大量神经元的放电，比较运动期间与之后的跨区通讯和编码质量；再用微电刺激检验区域间突触效能，最后让动物完成自由移动中的视觉检测任务，检验行为后果。
三、结果：运动期间与之后，视觉皮层到前额叶的通讯增强，前额叶神经元视觉诱发反应更大、群体编码更准确（视觉皮层本身没有同样提升）；相应地，运动后动物在视觉检测任务上表现更好。电刺激显示运动时区域间突触效能升高，提示这是通讯增强的生理基础。
四、意义：这说明“动起来”不只是看到更多画面，还会主动上调关键通路的增益，在刺激快速变化、决策时间窗很短的探索场景中保住知觉精度，对理解主动感知与运动—认知交互很有价值。

items.title_en: Structural and evolutionary insights into FcαμR recognition of polymeric immunoglobulins
items.title_zh: FcαμR 识别多聚免疫球蛋白的结构与演化机制
items.abstract_en: Polymeric immunoglobulins (pIgs) are central to adaptive immunity in jawed vertebrates. FcR is a bispecific pIg receptor that recognizes both IgM and IgA, but the molecular basis has been unclear. Here we determine cryo-EM structures of mammalian FcR bound to IgM or IgA and show that FcR engages each ligand in a 1:1 stoichiometry, with higher affinity for IgM. The FcR-binding site overlaps with those of pIgR, and also with the preferred FcR-binding site on IgM, yet distinct features distinguish FcR from both pIgR and FcR. Functionally, FcR efficiently internalizes both IgM and IgA through a pathway independent of the di-leucine motif. Structures of amphibian pIgR and FcR bound to IgM further shed light on the evolutionary diversification of the FcR/pIgR family. Together, these findings define the structural basis of FcR-mediated pIg recognition and provide a framework for understanding the evolution of pIg receptors.
items.abstract_zh: 多聚免疫球蛋白（pIgs）是有颌脊椎动物适应性免疫的核心。FcαμR 是可同时识别 IgM 与 IgA 的双特异性 pIg 受体，但其分子基础一直不清楚。本文测定哺乳动物 FcαμR 结合 IgM 或 IgA 的冷冻电镜结构，发现 FcαμR 以 1:1 化学计量比结合两种配体，且对 IgM 亲和力更高。其结合位点与 pIgR 的结合位点重叠，也与 IgM 上偏好的 FcμR 位点重叠，但独特结构特征使 FcαμR 区别于 pIgR 与 FcμR。功能上，FcαμR 经不依赖双亮氨酸基序的途径高效内吞 IgM 与 IgA。两栖类 pIgR 与 FcαμR 结合 IgM 的结构进一步揭示该受体家族的演化分化，为理解 pIg 识别及受体演化提供框架。
items.highlight_zh: 冷冻电镜揭示 FcαμR 以 1:1 比例双特异性结合 IgM 与 IgA 的结构基础
items.digest_zh:
「研究问题」IgM 与 IgA 以多聚体形式存在，是体液免疫的主力。机体靠一类多聚免疫球蛋白受体来转运和清除它们：pIgR 负责跨上皮运输，FcμR 只认 IgM，而 FcαμR 同时认 IgM 和 IgA。此前人们不清楚 FcαμR 如何在分子层面“一箭双雕”。
「方法」作者用冷冻电镜解析了哺乳动物 FcαμR 分别与 IgM、IgA 结合的复合物结构，并辅以结合亲和力与细胞内吞实验；还解析了两栖类 pIgR 与 FcαμR 结合 IgM 的结构用于比较。
「结果」FcαμR 与两种配体均以 1:1 结合，对 IgM 亲和力更高；在配体上，其结合位点与 pIgR 的位点重叠，也与 IgM 上 FcμR 偏好的位点重叠，但受体侧有独特结构特征加以区分。功能上，FcαμR 内吞 IgM 和 IgA 不依赖其胞内双亮氨酸基序，说明走的是非常规内化路径。
「意义」该工作给出了 pIg 识别的结构蓝图，并借两栖类结构揭示 FcR/pIgR 家族在演化中如何分化出不同特异性，为理解免疫球蛋白受体的功能与演化提供框架。

items.title_en: Can the Human Plastisphere Account for the Rise of Type 1 Diabetes: A Computational Molecular Mimicry Study
items.title_zh: 人类“塑料圈”能否解释 1 型糖尿病的上升：一项计算分子拟态研究
items.abstract_en: An increased incidence of childhood type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has been widely documented, but its pathophysiological origins are poorly understood. The post-World War II expansion of the plastics industry in the United States and elsewhere coincides with a marked increase in T1DM incidence; however, no pathophysiological mechanism has been proposed that could justify such a temporal correlation. Here, we leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence and protein structure prediction and binding to show that molecular mimicry is a plausible pathophysiological mechanism for plastic fragments to induce onset of T1DM for individuals with certain HLA haplotypes.
items.abstract_zh: 儿童 1 型糖尿病（T1DM）发病率上升已被广泛记录，但其病理生理起源仍不清楚。美国等地二战后塑料工业的扩张与 T1DM 发病率的显著上升在时间上高度重合，然而此前尚无病理生理机制能解释这种时间相关性。本文借助人工智能与蛋白质结构预测、结合预测的最新进展，表明分子拟态是一种可能的病理生理机制：对携带特定 HLA 单倍型的个体，塑料碎片可借此诱发 T1DM。
items.highlight_zh: AI 结构预测提示塑料碎片或经分子拟态诱发特定 HLA 人群的 1 型糖尿病
items.digest_zh:
「研究问题」过去几十年儿童 1 型糖尿病发病率明显上升，原因不明。一个耐人寻味的巧合是：二战后塑料产量的激增曲线与发病率上升曲线高度重合。但相关不等于因果，此前没有人提出可检验的机制。
「方法」作者提出“分子拟态”假说：塑料降解碎片可能模拟人体自身蛋白的某些片段，使免疫系统误认并攻击自身。研究利用 AI 蛋白质结构预测与蛋白—配体结合预测工具，比较塑料相关分子的表位与胰岛自身抗原的表位，并结合 HLA 单倍型分析易感人群。
「结果」计算显示，对携带特定 HLA 单倍型的个体，塑料碎片与自身抗原之间存在结构上可行的模拟关系，即分子拟态在机制上“说得通”。
「意义」这为塑料暴露与 T1DM 的时间相关性提供了首个可检验的病理生理假说，提示环境塑料可能是自身免疫的潜在触发因素。但需强调这只是纯计算结果，仍需流行病学与实验验证，不能据此断定塑料已确证致病。

items.title_en: Rhizobia transform legume nodules via native T-DNA transfer systems
items.title_zh: 根瘤菌通过天然 T-DNA 转移系统转化豆科植物根瘤
items.abstract_en: Agrobacteria can deliver transfer DNA (T-DNA) into plant cells, causing tumorous growth. This process, agrobacteria-mediated transformation (AMT), underlies plant genetic engineering and has been regarded as an evolutionary innovation specific to these pathogens. By screening 63,759 alphaproteobacterial genomes for T-DNA border sequences, we identify mini-T-DNAs in diverse rhizobial genera. Each typically encodes a single cargo, a RolB/RolC family protein or a distant rhizobial homologue. We show that native rhizobia-mediated transformation (RMT) systems deliver these mini-T-DNAs into the root nodules of common bean, pea, and chickpea, where the cargo genes are expressed, with no signal in adjacent root tissue. RMT systems share VirG-dependent activation of the core virulence regulon but respond to distinct upstream signals. Our genome screen identifies many additional candidate T-DNA transfer systems, and phylogenetic analysis places their genes into two of the many type IV secretion system (T4SS) clades. RMT systems occur in both clades, together with other systems unrelated to T-DNA transfer, and typically have an ancestral-like T4SS configuration. In contrast, AMT systems occupy a single subclade, consistent with later acquisition of their T4SS module. AMT and RMT thus represent two specialized outcomes of an older, more widespread capability for bacteria-to-plant DNA transfer.

items.title_en: High-throughput, single-cell-encoded colony imaging reveals infection-linked heterogeneity
items.title_zh: 高通量单细胞编码菌落成像揭示感染相关异质性
items.abstract_en: Phenotypic heterogeneity within bacterial populations shapes adaptation, antibiotic tolerance, and infection dynamics, yet colony-level quantification remains difficult at scale and on dark/selective media. We present HeteroTyper, an automated, high-throughput time-lapse platform that measures colony phenotypes across >100 plates per run on both transparent and dark media. HeteroTyper includes a ready-to-use computational pipeline that can be deployed on common plate-imaging setups and across agar types, delivering appearance times as a proxy for lag times, growth trajectories, colony size, intensity, and morphology from routine image series. Automated counts closely matched manual counts, supporting accuracy and scalability. Using Yersinia pseudotuberculosis as a model, HeteroTyper resolves phenotypic heterogeneity in vitro, with early and late phases showing broader appearance time distributions than mid-log phases. It also reveals organ-specific heterogeneity in vivo, with mesenteric lymph node isolates displaying the broadest appearance time distributions compared to spleen and liver. Appearance time was negatively associated with final colony size and intensity, linking growth initiation to downstream colony outcomes. Together, these distribution-level measurements indicate that bacterial adaptation during infection is compartmentalized by tissue microenvironments and prior history, and establish HeteroTyper as a practical, generalizable route to quantify infection-relevant phenotypic diversity on solid media at routine, high throughput.

items.title_en: Antibiotic-induced protein mislocalization drives hypervesiculation in Salmonella
items.title_zh: 抗生素诱导的蛋白错误定位驱动沙门氏菌囊泡过度形成
items.abstract_en: The incorporation of cytosolic proteins into bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) has remained mechanistically unresolved, as these proteins are normally excluded from vesiculation sites by the inner membrane (IM) barrier. Here, we show that antibiotic-induced envelope perturbation compromises this spatial barrier, enabling an aberrant interaction between proteins that are ordinarily segregated across cellular compartments and thereby promoting MV formation in Salmonella. Exposure to non-lethal cephalexin (LEX) induced robust hypervesiculation, accompanied by inhibition of the essential division penicillin binding protein (PBP) 3 and accumulation of the PBP5. Under envelope perturbing conditions, PBP5 accumulated at lateral sites associated with MV emergence and promoted periplasmic crowding independently of its catalytic activity. A cytosolic acyl carrier protein (ACP) emerged as a PBP5 interacting partner under LEX exposure, coinciding with cryogenic electron microscopy detected IM perturbation and aberrant ACP mislocalization. Formation of the PBP5 ACP complex promoted PBP5 accumulation, resulting in periplasmic crowding, progressive weakening of outer membrane peptidoglycan tethering, and ultimately MV formation. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism whereby stress-induced disruption of subcellular compartmentalization enables a non-canonical interaction between normally segregated proteins, driving hypervesiculation in Salmonella.

items.title_en: Phosphate-responsive ornithine lipid biosynthesis remodels outer membrane composition and contributes to polymyxin tolerance
items.title_zh: 磷酸盐响应性鸟氨酸脂质生物合成重塑外膜组成并促进多粘菌素耐受
items.abstract_en: Bacteria frequently encounter environments in which essential nutrients are limiting. Phosphate limitation constrains phospholipid synthesis and challenges maintenance of the cell envelope. While many Gram-negative bacteria respond by producing phosphorous-free membrane lipids, the mechanisms and consequences of this remodeling remain poorly understood in Enterobacterales. Here, we characterize the genetic and physiological basis of ornithine lipid (OL) biosynthesis in the opportunistic pathogens Enterobacter cloacae and Klebsiella pneumoniae. We show that OL biosynthesis depends on OlsF, a bifunctional acyltransferase that catalyzes both acylation steps required for OL synthesis. Phosphate limitation promotes OlsF-dependent OL accumulation through the PhoBR two-component system. Membrane fractionation revealed that OlsF-derived OLs are present in both membrane compartments but are enriched in the outer membrane. OlsF-dependent OL production enhances polymyxin tolerance during phosphate limitation, linking nutrient availability to changes in antimicrobial susceptibility. Together, these findings identify OlsF-dependent OL synthesis as a phosphate-responsive membrane remodeling pathway that reshapes outer membrane composition and influences the physiological properties of the Gram-negative cell envelope.

items.title_en: MoALE1, an ART-like effector, contributes to rice blast virulence through host immune suppression
items.title_zh: MoALE1，一种 ART 样效应因子，通过抑制宿主免疫促进稻瘟病致病性
items.abstract_en: Rice blast, caused by the hemibiotrophic fungus Magnaporthe oryzae, is one of the most destructive diseases affecting rice production worldwide. During infection, M. oryzae secretes effector proteins that suppress host immunity and facilitate colonization. Here, we characterized MoALE1, a predicted effector that is structurally similar to members of the heat-labile enterotoxin/cholera toxin family. Using a yeast secretion trap assay, we demonstrated that MoALE1 contains a functional signal peptide. A MoALE1-GFP fusion localized to the biotrophic interfacial complex, indicating that MoALE1 is a cytoplasmic effector. Expression analyses revealed that MoALE1 is expressed during biotrophy, from 16 to 48 h post-inoculation. Transient expression in Nicotiana benthamiana showed that MoALE1 suppresses BAX-mediated cell death, suggesting a role in host immune suppression. To investigate its contribution to pathogenicity, a{Delta} moale1 mutant was generated and evaluated in rice infection assays. Deletion of MoALE1 significantly reduced disease severity but did not affect fungal growth, stress tolerance, sporulation, appressorium development, host penetration, or early invasive growth. In contrast, infection by the {Delta}moale1 mutant resulted in enhanced host H2O2 accumulation and increased expression of ROS-associated defense genes. Together, these findings identify MoALE1 as a biotrophy-associated cytoplasmic effector that promotes rice blast pathogenicity by suppressing host immune responses and provide new insight into the function of ADP-ribosyltransferase (ART)-like effector candidates in M. oryzae .

items.title_en: Life on leaves left a lasting mark on the Methylobacterium core genome
items.title_zh: 叶面生活给甲基杆菌核心基因组留下持久印记
items.abstract_en: The extent to which core genomes reflect strictly vertical inheritance remains debated, particularly in ecologically diverse bacterial lineages. Here, we investigate the evolution of the core genome of Methylobacterium, a major leaf-associated bacterial genus, to assess how evolutionary signals vary across genes and whether they relate to functions involved in adaptation to life at the surface of plant leaves (the phyllosphere). Identifying 1,099 protein-coding core genes across 293 genomes, we combined gene tree comparisons, phylogenetic network reconstruction, nucleotide polymorphism patterns, and functional enrichment analyses. We found that most core genes show some deviation from the consensus phylogenetic tree. However, this discordance is not randomly distributed. Across all analytical approaches, genes showing the strongest deviations are consistently associated with functions linked to life in the phyllosphere, including anoxygenic photosynthesis, protection against UV and osmotic stress. These genes are often grouped into conserved clusters in the genome. In particular, a large cluster involved in anoxygenic photosynthesis, including bacteriochlorophyll and carotenoid biosynthesis, shows strong variation in its evolutionary history and organization across lineages, despite maintaining a conserved core structure. Similar patterns of phylogenetic incongruence and gene organization are observed across related Hyphomicrobiales inhabiting the phyllosphere, suggesting that these functions extend beyond Methylobacterium. Together, these results indicate that evolutionary heterogeneity within the core genome is concentrated in genes involved in key ecological functions. While alternative explanations cannot be excluded, these patterns are consistent with horizontal gene transfer contributing to the diversification of traits important for survival and adaptation in phyllosphere bacterial communities.

items.title_en: Unprecedented urban freshwater microviral survey highlights shift from sewage to river water communities
items.title_zh: 前所未有的城市淡水微型病毒调查揭示从污水到河水群落的转变
items.abstract_en: Microviruses are abundant yet still poorly resolved components of virosphere, particularly across urban freshwater continua. Here, we investigated complete microvirus genomes recovered from sewage water (SW), treated wastewater (TW), and river water (RW) along an urban SW TW RW continuum, providing an extensive genomic dataset of 18,449 complete genomes grouped into 825 genera. This catalog enabled a high-resolution assessment of microvirus diversity, taxonomy, and ecological distribution across anthropized aquatic compartments. All currently described microvirus orders were detected, with Gokushovirales dominating the dataset and Betagokushoviridae emerging as the most prevalent family in TW and RW samples. In contrast, Alpavirales were enriched in SW but strongly depleted after treatment, consistent with their association with gut-related bacterial hosts. Alpha- and beta-diversity analyses showed that water type was the main driver of microvirus community structure, whereas seasonal effects were weak and not robust under the hydrological conditions of the sampling year. Wastewater treatment plants thus acted as strong biological filters, reshaping viral assemblages and selecting compartment-specific microvirus populations. Finally, the pronounced and reproducible shifts observed across the continuum suggest that selected microvirus groups may serve as promising bioindicators of anthropogenic influence in freshwater systems.

items.title_en: Isolation of functional endogenous clathrin-coated vesicles and in vitro reconstitution of pure clathrin cages
items.title_zh: 功能性内源性网格蛋白包被囊泡的分离及纯网格蛋白笼的体外重构
items.abstract_en: Clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs) mediate key endocytic trafficking events, and dysfunction of CCVs is linked to multiple human diseases. Conventional centrifugation-based purification protocols can enrich endogenous CCVs but fail to eliminate intraluminal smooth vesicles (SVs) and co-isolated exosomes; these lipid contaminants reduce sample homogeneity and hinder high-resolution structural and proteomic analysis. Here, we present an integrated workflow to isolate biologically active endogenous CCVs from porcine brain and reconstitute homogeneous, SV-free clathrin cages. Crude CCVs are first enriched by differential and sucrose density gradient centrifugation to deplete the majority of exosomes. Clathrin cages are then depolymerized under alkaline conditions, allowing separation of soluble clathrin and adaptor proteins from SVs and residual lipid contaminants via ultracentrifugation. Purified coat proteins are reassembled in vitro into uniform clathrin cages. Functional assays confirm that purified CCVs retain Auxilin-Hsc70-dependent uncoating activity, and the enclosed SVs carry active vATPase proton pumps. This approach produces well-defined samples suitable for cryo-electron microscopy and mass spectrometry-based investigation of clathrin assembly and disassembly.

items.title_en: Disease-Causing Mutations Alter the Interplay Between Loop Dynamics and Catalysis in the Protein Tyrosine Phosphatases SHP-1 and SHP-2
items.title_zh: 致病突变改变蛋白酪氨酸磷酸酶 SHP-1 和 SHP-2 中环动力学与催化之间的相互作用
items.abstract_en: The protein tyrosine phosphatases (PTPs) SHP-1 and SHP-2 play complex roles in a variety of signaling pathways, including those involved in cancers and other diseases, making them important drug targets. These two PTPs have superimposable active sites, but different biological functions in vivo, including opposing roles in cancer development. Unique to these PTPs is the presence of two tandem Src homology 2 (SH2) domains, which regulate access to the phosphate-binding site in the catalytic domain through an autoinhibition mechanism. Studies of the allosteric regulation and dynamics of these PTPs, as well as associated drug discovery efforts, typically focus on autoinhibition rather than the dynamics of a catalytic loop in the phosphatase domain, the WPD-loop, which is essential for PTPase activity. However, recent deep mutational scanning data has demonstrated that oncogenic mutations also regulate WPD-loop motion in SHP-2. We provide here a detailed computational study of WPD-loop dynamics and catalysis in wild-type and mutant full-length and catalytic domain only SHP-1 and SHP-2, demonstrating that many oncogenic residues lie on the allosteric pathways regulating WPD-loop dynamics. Mutations at these positions alter WPD-loop dynamics, disrupting the active site and negatively impacting catalysis. Further, our simulations provide molecular insight into the link between the presence of the SH2 domains and loop motion in the catalytic domain, and, importantly, how it differs between the two PTPs. Taken together, our work showcases the impact of altered WPD-loop motion in disease-causing SHP-1 and SHP-2 variants, opening new strategies for selectively targeting these important therapeutic enzymes.

items.title_en: SeCAT (Sequence Consensus Amplicon Trimming): a simulation-informed Nextflow pipeline for cross-study harmonisation of 16S rRNA metabarcoding datasets
items.title_zh: SeCAT（序列一致性扩增子修剪）：一种基于模拟的 Nextflow 流程，用于 16S rRNA 宏条形码数据集的跨研究统一
items.abstract_en: Global syntheses of 16S rRNA metabarcoding data rely on combining datasets, yet amplicon sequence variants generated with different primer pairs can rarely be compared directly. Existing approaches correct batch effects statistically or aggregate taxonomically; none first establishes whether the sequences are positionally comparable. We present SeCAT (Sequence Consensus Amplicon Trimming), a Nextflow pipeline that maps every studys variants onto a 16S rRNA full-length reference alignment, determines the largest window shared across studies, and tests by simulation whether trimming to that window degrades community structure before any data are merged. Applied to thirteen marine studies sequenced with three primer sets, twelve converged on a consensus window with a median trimmed read length of 249 bp (9,582 alignment columns). Degradation tests across twelve studies and six taxonomic ranks (72 study-rank combinations) returned 31 passes, 38 cautions and three confirmed failures. Eleven studies (682 samples after filtering) were harmonised (trimmed to the window and merged), collapsing 20,891 primer-specific variants into 12,667 MetaASVs, trimmed sequences deduplicated across studies. Harmonisation preserved community structure at family level (Mantel r = 1.00; Procrustes m{superscript 2} < 0.001) without adding between-study variance (|{Delta}R{superscript 2}| < 0.001). Alpha diversity, including observed richness, was recovered across all levels (intraclass correlations 0.93-1.00), whereas sequence-level congruence was moderate (Procrustes m{superscript 2} = 0.52), as expected where between-study similarity at sequence level exists only after harmonisation. The harmonised output supports synthesis from aggregated ranks down to exact sequences. By establishing positional comparability before merging, SeCAT opens the archive of primer-fragmented 16S rRNA surveys to sequence-level synthesis.

items.title_en: PLATE: a global atlas of food metaplasmidomes
items.title_zh: PLATE：全球食品宏质粒组图谱
items.abstract_en: Plasmids play a central role in the acquisition and spread of genes underlying important traits in food-associated microorganisms. Although shotgun metagenomics has greatly expanded opportunities to study food microbiomes, their plasmid diversity remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we present the Plasmid Atlas of Food Ecosystems (PLATE), a curated global resource of food metaplasmidomes. Built from 4,690 food metagenomes spanning 55 countries and 17 categories, PLATE comprises a broad catalog (bPLATE) of 3,904,895 putative plasmid contigs (PPCs) and a refined catalog (rPLATE) of 213,474 PPCs, corresponding to 181,871 unique sequences. Both catalogs are complemented by curated sample metadata, host predictions, taxonomic assignments, and functional annotations covering antimicrobial resistance (AMR), protein families and KEGG orthologs, CRISPR-Cas systems, carbohydrate-active enzymes, and bioactive peptides. We demonstrate PLATE's utility through a case study of AMR genes detected on PPCs from food microbiomes. PLATE is freely accessible and enables users to interactively search for and download sequences, annotations, and associated metadata. By organizing plasmid-associated sequence diversity and functional potential across food ecosystems, PLATE provides a foundation for analyses of food metaplasmidomes.

items.title_en: TensorPLS: an R package for exploring molecular and temporal patterns in longitudinal omics data using PLS-DA
items.title_zh: TensorPLS：一个用于利用 PLS-DA 探索纵向组学数据中分子与时间模式的 R 包
items.abstract_en: Longitudinal omics datasets combine high-dimensional repeated measurements with missing observations, complicating supervised modelling and temporal interpretation. We present TensorPLS, an R package integrating missing-data handling, matrix-based partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), structured variable importance, subject-level nested cross-validation and downstream functional enrichment. Data are represented as subjects x features x time tensors. Missing values are handled by Tucker3 reconstruction or feature-time mean imputation, after which tensors are unfolded along the subject mode for PLS-DA. Cumulative variable importance in projection (VIP) scores are mapped to feature-time coordinates and summarised across time and cumulative PLS models. During nested cross-validation, imputation, component tuning, VIP-based feature selection and refitting are performed within training partitions. Full-cohort models are fitted separately for descriptive interpretation. We evaluated TensorPLS on two public longitudinal transcriptomic datasets using five-by-five nested cross-validation. In GSE68310 (109 subjects), Tucker3 reconstruction yielded Q2Y = 0.670, AUROC 0.971 and balanced accuracy 0.931. In GSE182616 (66 subjects), feature-time mean imputation yielded Q2Y = 0.294, AUROC 0.827 and balanced accuracy 0.756. Predictive metrics were calculated from pooled outer held-out predictions. TensorPLS supports predictive assessment, functional enrichment of selected genes and temporal interpretation of model-assigned feature importance.

items.title_en: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
items.title_zh: 揭示单细胞与空间组学中的跨信号相互作用
items.abstract_en: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation-position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-{beta} response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.

items.title_en: Disentangling Context-Specific Alzheimer's Disease Progression Signatures through an Explainable AI Framework
items.title_zh: 通过可解释 AI 框架厘清情境特异性阿尔茨海默病进展特征
items.abstract_en: Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression involves stage-dependent transcriptional changes that are often masked by dominant cellular and biological variation. Here, we present ADVISE (Alzheimer's Disease Variational Isolation of Signal Embeddings), an interpretable deep generative framework designed to disentangle Braak stage-associated transcriptional signals from background biological variation through separate latent representations. Using explainable AI, ADVISE prioritizes genes and pathways contributing to the disease-specific representation. Applying ADVISE to large-scale single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from the human prefrontal cortex, we identify shared and context-specific signatures of AD progression across global, sex-specific, and cell-type-specific analyses, revealing convergent molecular programs involving synaptic transmission, HSF1-associated proteostatic stress responses, and SLIT/ROBO axon guidance. Notably, ADVISE prioritizes ROBO2 as a progression-associated candidate in excitatory neurons. Experimental validation using CRISPR activation in hiPSC-derived excitatory neurons demonstrates that ROBO2 activation reduces the phosphorylated Tau-to-total Tau ratio. ADVISE thus reveals context-dependent molecular signatures of AD progression and bridges human single-cell discoveries with experimental validation of candidate regulators of AD pathology.

items.title_en: Unified cell segmentation for spatial transcriptomics via transcript reassignment
items.title_zh: 通过转录本重分配实现空间转录组学的统一细胞分割
items.abstract_en: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression as individually localized molecules on imaging-based platforms or as counts in subcellular bins on sequencing-based platforms, and both must be assigned to cells before cell-level analysis. Existing segmentation methods focus on delineating cell boundaries, yet transcripts that diffuse beyond their cell of origin, fall where cells overlap, or lie in bins that cells only partially cover are still misassigned. Here we present Tracel, a two-stage optimal transport framework that assigns spatial observations to cells under the guidance of a matched single-cell RNA-sequencing reference. Tracel first aligns reference cells to spatial cells to estimate the expected expression profile at each cell location, and then maps transcripts to cells against these profiles. The same formulation assigns transcripts from imaging-based platforms (e.g., Xenium, CosMx) and bin counts from sequencing-based platforms (e.g., Visium HD). Across five human datasets spanning three platforms and three tissues, Tracel improves the separation of cell types over existing methods, assigning cell-type markers to their correct cells, retaining more cell-intrinsic transcripts and reducing contamination from neighboring cells. Tracel also preserves variation within cell types, yielding more accurate differential expression across spatial locations, and its expression profiles attribute ligand-receptor interactions to the correct cell-type pairs in cell-cell communication analysis. Tracel can enter the segmentation workflow at different stages, either refining an existing segmentation or segmenting cells starting from nucleus segmentation.

items.title_en: Long read sequencing reveals changes in measured isoform structure and abundance due to RNA processing
items.abstract_en: Oxford Nanopore Technology enables direct RNA sequencing without reverse transcription (RT) and cDNA sequencing without PCR amplification, allowing investigation of how RNA preparation protocols bias sequencing data. PCR amplification is known to introduce biases related to expression levels, transcript lengths, and GC content. However, biases introduced by RT have been described more recently and their quantification remains more elusive. Using seven cell line datasets from SG-NEx, we compared nanopore sequencing of direct RNA, direct cDNA, and PCR-amplified cDNA. We identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes and isoforms between protocols, indicating significant changes in observed expression. Differentially expressed isoforms displayed expected amplification biases, and further we observed decreased PCR counts associated with higher m6A methylation levels on native RNA. We also found differential transcript usage in hundreds of genes across cell lines, showing substantial changes in measured isoform proportions between protocols. Analysis of structural differences between isoforms that switch dominance revealed that while some events involve simple RNA fragmentation, most involve complex structural differences including novel junctions (e.g. exon skipping, intron retention). Compared to non-DTU genes, inserted introns (exitrons) were significantly more common after RT and amplification. Furthermore, visualisation of raw coverage data proved crucial for qualitative validation of experimental findings.

items.title_en: STRUCTURAL PLASTICITY ALLOWS DOUBLECORTIN AND DRUG-STABILIZED MICROTUBULES TO ACCOMMODATE EACH OTHER
items.abstract_en: Microtubule architecture and dynamics are modulated by small molecules, but how these compounds alter lattice properties and interactions with cellular regulators remains incompletely understood. We used the neuronal microtubule-associated protein doublecortin (DCX), previously reported to preferentially recognize 13-protofilament microtubules, to probe lattices stabilized by different taxanes, including the fluorescent taxane Fchitax-3. We show that DCX binds 15-protofilament Fchitax-3-stabilized microtubules, demonstrating that DCX is not a specific marker of 13-protofilament architecture. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that the fluorescent moiety of Fchitax-3 inserts into inter-protofilament lateral contacts, explaining its effects on microtubule architecture and dynamics. DCX binds Fchitax-3 microtubules through its N-terminal DC domain, which accommodates the narrower inter-protofilament binding site in the 15-protofilament lattice. Remarkably, although Fchitax-3 induces the longitudinal lattice expansion characteristic of taxanes, DCX remodels its binding site towards its preferred compacted configuration. Thus, taxanes can modify microtubule structure in distinct ways while preserving lattice plasticity and the capacity to undergo conformational remodelling by microtubule-associated proteins. This contrasts with the comparatively rigid lattice of GMPCPP-stabilized microtubules. Consequently, interpretations of microtubule lattice states based on comparisons between taxane- and GMPCPP-stabilized microtubules may conflate structural differences with different degrees of lattice plasticity. Our findings establish the microtubule lattice as a malleable structural substrate whose drug-induced conformations can be further remodelled by cellular binding partners.

items.title_en: Pervasive chromothripsis drives pleural mesothelioma to impact gene function and patient survival
items.abstract_en: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a tumour type showing high structural complexity but the full spectrum of variants present and their impacts are poorly understood. We comprehensively describe the mutational landscape of mesothelioma, exploiting a large (N=443) cohort profiling the tumour genome and transcriptome in parallel. We find that the majority of candidate driver variants are mediated by copy number alterations (CNAs) and discover high frequencies of complex rearrangements across most tumours, dominated by chromothripsis (74% of tumours) and chromoplexy (59%). Chromothripsis contributes to significant CNA hotspots to delete known PM tumour suppressor genes such as CDKN2A, NF2 and BAP1, thought to be among the earliest events in PM development; and the presence of chromothripsis is associated with significantly worse patient survival. We also discover multi-faceted crosstalk between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes during PM evolution, involving alterations to both genomes, and mitochondrial expression changes associated with subtypes and chromothripsis.

items.title_en: Clinical and Social Determinants of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Optimization in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
items.abstract_en: Background: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF has been shown to improve outcomes, with higher GDMT scores at hospital discharge being associated with lower mortality, fewer rehospitalizations and reduced healthcare costs. Yet, disparities in the utilization of GDMT remain. In this study, we examined the effect of various clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic factors on the utilization of GDMT in HFrEF patients referred to Cardiology in a tertiary care safety net hospital, using a standardized GDMT scoring system. Methods: We conducted a single-center cross-sectional retrospective analysis of patients who had an index HFrEF 40% diagnosis between January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2024, and who were referred to Cardiology at a tertiary care safety net hospital. Baseline characteristics, laboratory investigations, health care utilization, and GDMT score data were extracted at the ambulatory care visit nearest to 90 days from the index HF diagnosis. GDMT score ranges from 0 to 9 factored in doses of beta-blocker (BB), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker (ACEi/ARB), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI), isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine (ISDN/HYD). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to examine associations between low GDMT scores (0-4) nearest to 90 days from new onset HFrEF diagnosis and several clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic variables. Results: In 200 patients meeting entry criteria, mean age was 62.7 years, 64.0% were male, 47.5% were classified as white and 42.0% as Black. 39.5% had a low GDTM score (<5). The following were less likely to be associated with low GDMT score: diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR: 0.41, 95%CI=0.18-0.91) and frequent medical appointments (adjusted OR: 0.37, 95% CI=0.25-0.54), while higher serum eGFR was more likely to be associated with low GDMT score (adjusted OR: 1.02, 95%CI=1.00-1.03). There was no significant association between GDMT score and age, sex, race, or payer status. Conclusion: In patients with HFrEF referred to Cardiology in our safety net tertiary care center, higher utilization of GDMT at 90 days was achieved in those who have diabetes mellitus, more frequent medical appointments, or lower serum eGFR. There was no difference in GDMT utilization according to age, sex, race, or payer status predictive of lower GDMT scores. Contrary to findings from previous studies, no significant differences were observed across demographic or payer groups, emphasizing the role of healthcare access and utilization.

items.title_en: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction - real world outcomes
items.abstract_en: Aims: To evaluate the effectiveness of GLP-1 RAs on clinical outcomes in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods and results: In this retrospective observational cohort study, all adults with diabetes mellitus and HFrEF between 2014 and 2025 were identified. Patients treated with GLP-1 RAs were matched to controls using stratified exact matching. The primary outcome was a composite of heart failure hospitalization or all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were estimated using nonparametric bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations) to derive risk ratios, NNT estimates, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Time-to-event analyses using Cox proportional hazards models were performed as a validation analysis. Among 7,878 patients with HFrEF, 793 (10.1%) patients who initiated GLP-1 RA therapy after HF diagnosis were matched to 1,825 controls. GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization or death, with risk ratios of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.42-0.77) at 12 months and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.61-0.85) at 36 months. The combination of high baseline event rates and substantial relative risk reduction translated into remarkably low NNT values in the overall population, with an NNT of 17 (95% CI: 11-33) at 1 year and 13 (95% CI: 8-25) at 3 years. Post hoc subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent effects across clinical subgroups, with no significant heterogeneity observed. Conclusion: In this large real-world cohort of diabetic patients with HFrEF, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy, in addition to guideline-directed medical therapy, was associated with a lower risk of death or heart failure hospitalization.

items.title_en: Periodontitis and Associated Factors Among Dental Outpatients at Tertiary Hospitals in Dhaka
items.abstract_en: Objective: To identify the factors associated with periodontitis among dental outpatient departments at tertiary hospitals in Dhaka. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 227 patients from dental outpatient departments of three tertiary-level hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh by intra-oral examinations and in-person interviews using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire through Simplified Oral Hygiene Index (OHI-S) and the Community Periodontal Index (CPI) component of the CPITN. Results: About 55% were classified as having periodontitis. Both diabetes mellitus (p < 0.05) and harmful oral habits (smoking, smokeless tobacco, and constant tooth picking) were significantly associated with periodontitis (p < 0.05). Participants with diabetes had 2.87 times higher odds of periodontitis (OR: 2.870, 95% CI: 1.516-5.441). The odds of having periodontitis were 7.27 times higher for smokeless tobacco users (OR: 7.271, 95% CI: 3.609-14.651), and smokers had 3.69-fold higher odds of periodontitis (OR: 3.687, 95% CI: 1.701-7.988). A strong positive correlation was observed between poor oral hygiene status and the presence of periodontitis (r = 0.947, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Diabetes, smoking and poor oral hygiene are key determinants of periodontitis which underscore the need for targeted oral health promotion, regular screening and integration of periodontal care into geriatric services. Keywords: Periodontitis; Oral hygiene; Tobacco use; Diabetes mellitus

items.title_en: The origin of the MV Hondius Andes outbreak
items.abstract_en: In April-July 2026, Andes virus (ANDV) caused an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulting in 12 confirmed cases and three deaths. Before symptom onset, the index case had travelled through hantavirus-endemic regions of Chile and Argentina, leaving the geographic origin of infection unresolved. We conducted phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses using newly generated ANDV genomes from human cases and rodent reservoirs to investigate the likely origin of the outbreak. Through phylogenetic analyses, we show that the outbreak genome falls within a geographically structured lineage spanning southern Chile and Argentine Andean Patagonia. Using phylogeographic reconstructions across all three segments, integrated with the index case's travel itinerary, we identified the Tolten-Lanco area of southern Chile as the most likely geographic origin of the outbreak genome, with two candidate locations accounting for >98% of the posterior support. However, the index case visited this area 62-66 days before symptom onset, exceeding the conventionally reported ANDV incubation period of 7-42 days. Thus, while genomic evidence supports a southern Chilean origin of the outbreak genome, the timing and circumstances of transmission to the index case remain unresolved.

items.title_en: Determinants of Binge Drinking Among Current Alcohol Drinkers: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2013 Health and Welfare Survey
items.abstract_en: This cross sectional analytical study examined the prevalence and determinants of binge drinking (BD) among current alcohol drinkers (CAD) aged 20 years and older in Thailand (N = 52,847). Data from the Health and Welfare Surveys (HWS) were analyzed using chi square tests and multiple logistic regression. In 2013, nearly 69% of the 5,445 current drinkers reported BD. Multivariable analyses indicated significantly higher odds of BD among men (AOR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.90-2.66; p < 0.001), younger adults (AOR range: 1.50-1.90; p < 0.001), individuals with household housing expenses (AOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.01-1.39; p < 0.05), and those with secondary/vocational or tertiary education (AOR range: 1.35-1.36; p < 0.05). Smoking was also associated with elevated odds of BD (AOR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.23-1.62; p < 0.001). In contrast, respondents in high income groups had lower odds (AOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.54-0.87; p < 0.01), as did residents of non metropolitan areas compared with Bangkok (AOR range: 0.44-0.59; p < 0.01). In conclusion, binge drinking affected over half of Thai drinkers and was strongly linked to demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and behavioral factors. The frequent co-occurrence of alcohol use and smoking underscores the clustering of non-communicable disease risks, highlighting the need for integrated dual-cessation programs. While cross-sectional design and 2013 data limitations apply, these findings provide actionable evidence for public health agencies to implement targeted screening and intervention strategies for high-risk populations.

items.title_en: Identifying Register-Based Severity Trajectories in Anorexia Nervosa: Associations with Polygenic Scores, Psychiatric and Somatic Conditions
items.abstract_en: Importance. Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe psychiatric disorder with heterogeneous outcomes and elevated mortality. Characterizing severity trajectories may improve early risk stratification and targeted intervention. Objective. To identify AN severity trajectories using a register-based severity index (AN-RSI) and examine their associations with polygenic scores (PGS), preceding (prior to AN diagnosis) as well as subsequent (beyond 5 years post AN diagnosis) psychiatric and somatic disorders. Design. Population-based cohort study. Setting. Nationwide study in Denmark. Participants. Individuals born between 1963 and 2007 with diagnosed AN (N = 9534 individuals). Genetic data were available in a subsample (N = 5126). Exposures. Forty-one PGS indexing traits relevant to AN, and psychiatric and somatic disorders prior to AN diagnosis. Main Outcomes and Measures. AN-RSI trajectories, psychiatric, and somatic disorders beyond 5 years post AN diagnosis. Results. Three trajectories were identified: "low and stable" (32.6%), "medium and stable" (53.5%), and "high increasing" (14.0%). The "low and stable" group was used as the comparison group for all analyses. Each 1 standard deviation (SD) increase in AN PGS corresponded with 13% greater odds of following the "high increasing" trajectory. Increases in BMI and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) PGS corresponded with 15% and 14% lower odds of following the "high increasing" trajectory, respectively. No preceding psychiatric or somatic disorders were significantly associated with trajectory membership. In contrast, subsequent psychiatric and somatic disorders were more likely in individuals following the "high increasing" trajectory with odds ratios ranging between 1.7 (ADHD) and 3.7 (psychoactive substance dependence) for psychiatric disorders and between 1.6 (poor fetal growth of child) and 4 (microcytic anemia) for somatic disorders. Conclusions and Relevance. Our findings demonstrate that individuals with AN follow distinct severity trajectories that are associated with differences in polygenic risk and post-diagnostic morbidity patterns but not with pre-diagnosis psychiatric or somatic morbidity. As the field progresses, incorporating PGS into comprehensive assessments at first presentation may aid in early identification, personalized intervention, and resource allocation for individuals at higher risk of developing a severe illness trajectory.

items.title_en: Spatial distribution and factors associated with unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia: Evidence from the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey
items.abstract_en: Unmet need for family planning contributes to unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortions, and preventable maternal and child deaths, and remains high in sub-Saharan Africa. In Zambia, national estimates may conceal important geographic inequalities.
