We assessed the spatial distribution of, and factors associated with, unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS), including 12,133 women aged 15-49 years. Survey-weighted logistic regression, accounting for the stratified two-stage cluster design, was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Global spatial autocorrelation was assessed with Morans I, local hotspots with the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic, and spatial clusters with a purely spatial Bernoulli scan statistic in SaTScan. The weighted prevalence of unmet need was 27.0% (95% CI: 25.7-28.3%), ranging from 23.8% in Central to 31.6% in North-Western Province. Unmet need was spatially clustered (Morans I = 0.142, p = 0.018), with hotspots mainly in Lusaka, Southern, North-Western, and Northern provinces; SaTScan detected a primary cluster in Lusaka (observed-to-expected ratio 1.42, p < 0.001). Women in union (AOR 2.33, 95% CI: 1.90-2.86) and never-married women (AOR 2.20, 95% CI: 1.69-2.86) had higher odds of unmet need than formerly married women, as did women with five or more children compared with none (AOR 3.05, 95% CI: 2.25-4.13). Lower odds were observed among women aged 35-49 years (AOR 0.65, 95% CI: 0.52-0.83), women in the richest wealth quintile (AOR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.45-0.86), employed women (AOR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.64-0.84) and urban residents (AOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.68-0.95). Unmet need for family planning in Zambia is high, geographically clustered and socially patterned. Family planning programmes should prioritise hotspot areas, particularly Lusaka, Southern and North-Western provinces, while targeting younger, higher-parity and poorer women.

items.title_en: Biomarkers of ageing and lung function trajectory: a multi-omics study in a UK birth cohort
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accelerated biological ageing and cellular senescence are pathogenically implicated in COPD and may represent therapeutic targets. Adverse early-life lung function trajectories offer opportunities to prevent COPD but their relationship with epigenetic and proteomic ageing biomarkers remains unexplored. We investigated using conventional epidemiological and Mendelian randomisation (MR) methods. METHODS: Outcomes were the two lowest of five FEV1 trajectories (Persistently Low and Below Average) previously identified using latent profile analysis (ages 8-30) in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children. Exposures included nine measures of blood-derived epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and thirteen senescence-associated plasma proteins (ages 7-9). We used logistic regression to estimate odds of lower trajectory membership by exposure and bidirectional one-sample MR to investigate causation. RESULTS: Higher plasma CXCL10 (OR 1.29 per SD; 95% CI 1.03, 1.57), IL6 (OR 1.29; 1.03, 1.57) and IL33 (OR 1.23; 1.04, 1.44) were associated with Persistently Low lung function trajectory, with little evidence for associations between EAA and lower trajectories. MR provided little evidence that genetically predicted plasma proteins influenced risk of lower trajectories, but lower genetically proxied childhood FEV1 predicted higher plasma CXCL10 at ages 9 ({beta} -0.34; -0.65, -0.03) and 24 ({beta} -0.38; -0.67, -0.08). INTERPRETATION: Childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33, but not EAA, predict low lung function trajectory into early adulthood. Lower childhood lung function may causally relate to persistently increased plasma CXCL10. Future research should investigate IL33 as a potential therapeutic target in low lung function trajectory and persistent systemic inflammation as a mechanism for associated multimorbidity.

items.title_en: Symptom variability and treatment response in pernicious anaemia: a longitudinal daily symptom tracking study
items.abstract_en: Pernicious Anaemia is an autoimmune-mediated disorder of vitamin B12 absorption, managed using fixed-interval vitamin B12 replacement regimens. Despite treatment, many patients report persistent or recurrent symptoms, suggesting substantial inter-individual variability in treatment response. More tailored approaches may therefore be needed to reduce symptom burden and improve quality of life. This prospective observational study used high-frequency longitudinal digital symptom monitoring to characterise symptom dynamics and heterogeneity in treatment response. UK adults with pernicious anaemia, recruited via the Pernicious Anaemia Society, self-reported daily symptoms (severity 0-10) and vitamin B12 treatments over three months. Analyses quantified within- and between-person variability, injection-aligned symptom response kinetics, and differences in treatment response by injection frequency. Sixty-eight participants were included in the longitudinal analyses, providing >5,100 person-days of symptom data over a mean of 76 days (SD 28). Most symptom variance was attributable to stable between-person differences (ICC range, 0.58-0.80), indicating the persistence of individual symptom phenotypes. Vitamin B12 injections were followed by rapid symptom improvement, although magnitude and timing varied markedly by symptom domain. Seventy-one percent of participants were classified as responders for composite symptom burden (median 4.65 to 2.36; p<0.001), while 29% showed no meaningful multisystem improvement (3.59 to 3.58; p=0.63). Cognitive symptoms improved earliest, typically within 24-72 hours; fatigue and pain responses peaked at 3-5 days, and neuro-sensory symptoms at 4-6 days. Responses clustered within individuals, indicating distinct responder phenotypes. Overall symptom burden improved most among participants receiving monthly injections, whereas those injecting weekly or more often had higher pre-injection burden and smaller improvements. These findings suggest that fixed-interval vitamin B12 replacement may not adequately reflect individual variation in symptom recurrence and treatment response. High-frequency digital symptom monitoring may provide a practical framework for characterising these patterns and for evaluating more individualised, symptom-guided vitamin B12 management.

items.title_en: Modulating Amygdala Responses in Major Depressive Disorder using Naturalistic Neurofeedback with Emotional Faces
items.abstract_en: Emotion regulation is critical to mental health, and its disruption can lead to psychiatric conditions such as major depressive disorder (MDD). MDD encompasses diverse symptoms, including anhedonia and anxiety, which may be associated with distinct patterns of altered neural activity. Interventions that address the neural mechanisms underlying these symptom dimensions may improve treatment efficacy. We investigated an adaptive, naturalistic real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging neurofeedback paradigm designed to differentially target anhedonia and anxiety through bidirectional amygdala regulation. Unlike conventional abstract feedback, our approach used emotional faces whose expressions changed dynamically according to ongoing amygdala activity, embedding neural self-regulation within a socially relevant emotional context. In this parallel-group study, 21 patients with MDD received one of two neurofeedback conditions. In the Happy-up group, patients attempted to increase amygdala activity by making a neutral face happier to enhance positive emotional responding. In the Fear-down group, patients attempted to decrease amygdala activity by making a fearful face less fearful to reduce negative emotional reactivity. Both groups showed the expected pattern of neural regulation during neurofeedback, with greater amygdala activity during Happy upregulation and decreasing amygdala activity during Fear downregulation. Following the intervention, patients showed reductions in depression severity, anxiety, and anhedonia, and more positive evaluations of neutral and happy faces. However, improvements in anhedonia and anxiety did not differ significantly between groups. These findings show bidirectional amygdala regulation through naturalistic neurofeedback in MDD. Although symptom-specific clinical effects were not established, the observed clinical improvements underscore the therapeutic potential of this approach.

items.title_en: Knowledge, attitudes and behaviours related to tick awareness and prevention among users of urban green spaces: insights from stakeholder focus groups
items.abstract_en: Abstract Background: Ticks in the UK can transmit pathogens that lead to diseases in humans, including Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. Expanding tick populations and increasing human use of urban green spaces may elevate exposure risk. Public health advice exists, but little is known about how this guidance is understood and applied by users of urban environments. Methods: Four stakeholder focus groups were conducted with professionals involved in tick fieldwork in urban green spaces. Discussions explored interactions with the public, perceived awareness, behaviours, and views on communication. Data were analysed thematically using an approach informed by the Framework Method. Results: Stakeholders reported substantial variation in public awareness of ticks, influenced by prior exposure to rural environments and local knowledge. Misinformation, particularly around tick removal, was common. Signage was rarely observed in urban green spaces, and views on its effectiveness were mixed. Participants emphasised the need to balance risk communication with reassurance and highlighted the importance of age-appropriate education. Conclusions: Insights from stakeholders underline the importance of targeted, context specific public health messaging in urban settings. Priorities include identifying groups with lower awareness, addressing misinformation, designing balanced communication materials, evaluating the effectiveness of signage, and integrating education for children and families.

items.title_en: From telling to receiving: the disclosure-and-services cascade after childhood sexual abuse across 15 low- and middle-income countries
items.abstract_en: Most children who experience sexual abuse in low- and middle-income countries never receive formal help, but few studies have followed survivors through the steps from telling someone to receiving services. In this pooled cross-sectional analysis, we combined 15 nationally representative Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS) fielded between 2013 and 2024 in sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and Eastern Europe to describe this disclosure-and-services cascade and the factors associated with each step. The analytic sample comprised 3,608 respondents aged 18-24 years who reported sexual abuse before age 18 (2,852 female, 756 male). We estimated survey-weighted proportions for four steps: told anyone, knew where to seek formal help, sought help (among those who knew), and received help (among those who sought it). Design-based logistic regression with country fixed effects estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for individual, family, and community factors. Overall, 47.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 44.4-49.7) of survivors had told anyone and 34.8% (32.2-37.5) knew where to seek formal help. Of those who knew (n = 1,208), 24.8% (20.9-29.1) sought help, and of those who sought help (n = 339), 81.9% (75.9-86.7) received it. In total, 7.0% (5.7-8.5) of survivors received formal help; this proportion ranged from 0.9% to 26.3% across countries. Compared with male survivors, female survivors were more likely to tell anyone (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.73-3.05) and less likely to know where to seek help (aOR 0.68, 0.50-0.93); among survivors who knew where to go, female survivors were more likely to seek help (aOR 2.66, 1.39-5.09). Knowing where to seek help was more likely with older age, more schooling, and a living mother. Survivors who had ever married or cohabited were less likely to have told anyone (aOR 0.75, 0.58-0.96). No factor other than sex was associated with seeking help among those who knew where to go. Most survivors are lost before they reach a service: two in three do not know where to go, and three in four of those who know ultimately do not seek help. Once survivors seek help, most receive it. Interventions should make services known to young people, particularly those with less schooling, and address the barriers that keep survivors, especially young men, from using services they know about.

items.title_en: Utility of Rt epidemic trend categories for influenza surveillance: alignment with observed emergency department trends across two influenza seasons in the United States
items.abstract_en: CDC has estimated the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) for influenza in the United States since 2023, translating the posterior probability that Rt exceeds one, P(R_t>1), into epidemic trend categories (growing, likely growing, not changing, likely declining, declining). If Rt reliably indicates infection dynamics, growing or declining trends should precede corresponding changes in influenza-related emergency department (ED) visits, accounting for the lag between infection and care-seeking. However, because these categories reflect confidence in the direction of change rather than magnitude, their alignment with the corresponding trends ED activity measures is unclear. We compared weekly Rt epidemic trend categories to observed ED trends from the National Syndromic Surveillance Program across the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza seasons, using three thresholds to define observed trends at different magnitudes ([≥]0.1% difference, [≥]0.5% difference, [≥]5% relative change between consecutive weeks), comparing Rt trends to observed trends the following week. We assessed categorical alignment and calibration between P(R_t>1) and observed trends. Alignment was moderate overall, strongest for growing and declining categories under the 5% relative change threshold (61% aligned) and weakest under the 0.5% difference threshold (38.2% aligned); calibration was similarly best under the 5% relative change threshold. Misalignment concentrated around epidemic inflection points and periods of low influenza activity. Rt epidemic trend categories showed moderate, threshold-dependent alignment with observed ED activity, reflecting a combination of real-time model error and misalignment between direction-based and magnitude-based surveillance metrics. Defining categories based on Rt magnitude could improve correspondence with size-based change indicators and strengthen their utility for real-time monitoring.

items.title_en: Effects of Weighted Seated Core Exercises on Immediate Postural Stability in Healthy Young Adults: An Exploratory Study
items.abstract_en: Objectives: This exploratory study investigated whether low-load, seated core exercises could produce immediate improvements in standing balance among healthy young adults, aiming to provide a foundation for safe, early-stage rehabilitation protocols. Methods: Ten healthy males performed seated core exercises consisted of alternating hip flexion 5 times per side while seated and maintaining bilateral shoulder flexion at 120-degree shoulder flexion under four load conditions: upper-limb weight only, a 400-g empty box, a 1-kg ball, and a 2-kg ball. Immediately following the exercise, participants performed a 10-s single-leg stance. Transversus abdominis (TrA) thickness was measured via wireless ultrasound at baseline, post-exercise, and during the stance. Center of pressure (CoP) sway was recorded concurrently to evaluate postural stability. Results: Left-side TrA thickness during stance increased significantly under the 1-kg and 2-kg load conditions compared to baseline (p 0.05). A moderate positive correlation (rho = 0.43, p = 0.002) was found between right-side TrA thickness and CoP sway velocity during the single-leg stance. Conclusions: Low-load, seated core exercises do not yield immediate enhancements in standing stability in healthy populations. The results suggest that increased TrA thickness during a balance task may correlate with heightened postural instability rather than improved balance control. Further research is needed to determine whether these findings translate to clinical populations with impaired physical fitness.

items.title_en: Association between blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio and kidney stones: A cross-sectional study based on NHANES
items.abstract_en: Kidney stones are a disorder in which urinary solutes precipitate to form crystalline aggregates in the urinary space. The blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio (BAR), a common inflammatory indicator, has an unclear association with kidney stones. Using NHANES 2007-2020 data, we compared baseline characteristics between kidney stone formers and controls and evaluated the BAR-stone relationship via weighted multivariate logistic regression (WMLR), restricted cubic splines (RCS), stratification analyses, and XGBoost, with validation in an independent external cohort. Twenty baseline features, including BAR and age, differed significantly between groups (P 1, P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses revealed stable associations in females (OR = 1.10, P < 0.001), low vitamin A intake (OR = 1.10, P < 0.001), high water intake (OR = 1.11, P < 0.001), age < 50 years (OR = 1.14, P < 0.01), and education less than high school (OR = 1.11, P < 0.01). XGBoost identified BAR and water intake as prominent risk factors (AUC = 0.658). External validation confirmed a positive association (Model 1 OR = 1.029, 95% CI 1.016-1.043; Model 2 OR = 1.030, 95% CI 1.016-1.044; Model 3 OR = 1.029, 95% CI 1.015-1.045; all P < 0.001), and RCS confirmed a nonlinear dose-response relationship (nonlinear P = 0.0006). Subgroups aged [≥] 60 years, males, and females showed significant associations (ORs = 1.027-1.034). In XGBoost, BAR was the most important predictor (Gain = 0.265). These findings reveal a significant association between BAR and kidney stones, offering theoretical insights for prevention and risk stratification; BAR may serve as a valuable marker in kidney stone management.

items.title_en: CLIN-SUMM: Incremental Longitudinal Summarization of Clinical Notes Enables Scalable Representation and Early Disease Prediction
items.title_zh: CLIN-SUMM：临床笔记的增量纵向摘要实现可扩展表示与早期疾病预测
items.abstract_en: Electronic health records contain years of longitudinal clinical notes rich in evolving patient information, yet their volume, redundancy, and fragmentation limit clinical usability and scalable modeling. We present CLIN-SUMM (Clinical Longitudinal Insight from Notes using Summarization), a framework that restructures summarization as a longitudinal representation problem. Rather than collapsing histories into static summaries, CLIN-SUMM incrementally constructs structured, categorized, date-partitioned patient representations, summarizing only newly documented information at each encounter while preserving temporal fidelity without access to future data. This standardized representation can be computed once and reused across downstream tasks, thereby decoupling narrative processing from prediction. Across 12,356 Massachusetts General Hospital patients, CLIN-SUMM achieved 75% word reduction while maintaining high clinician-rated correctness and completeness. Using dementia as a case study, fine-tuning Clinical ModernBERT on CLIN-SUMM summaries yielded AUROC 0.84 for diagnosis and outperformed raw notes for 3-year risk prediction (AUROC 0.66 vs. 0.63). Combining summary-based predictions with structured EHR variables improved 3-year prediction to AUROC 0.69, reaching 0.74 among patients younger than 75 years, with longitudinal analyses demonstrating progressive risk separation years before a formal diagnosis. CLIN-SUMM summaries also enabled efficient extraction of longitudinal medication trajectories, complementing structured EHR data by recovering medication information documented in notes, with high dose agreement for matched records. CLIN-SUMM provides a scalable representation layer for clinical review and longitudinal machine learning, enhancing disease modeling, risk prediction, and other longitudinal reasoning tasks.

items.title_en: Cross-reactive antibody and functional T-cell responses to Bundibugyo virus induced by Zaire ebolavirus vaccination and infection
items.abstract_en: Background There is no licensed specific vaccine against the current Ebola Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbeak affecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo. However, clinical evaluations of a licensed Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) vaccine have just launched. It remains unclear whether EBOV infection or vaccination generate cross-reactive immunity against BDBV. Methods We quantified CD4 and CD8 T-cell magnitude, polyfunctionality, and cytotoxicity after 8-day expansion with EBOV, BDBV, Sudan (SUDV), or Marburg (MARV) GP peptide pools, and measured GP-binding antibodies by multiplex assay, in recipients of Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo (n=10), single-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (n=10), or two-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (n=8) (NCT02876328), and in EVD survivors sampled approximately 3 years after infection (n=10). Findings Fourteen days after completion of each licensed vaccine regimen, median BDBV-reactive CD4 responses were 9.8% [IQR:8.9-14.0] after single-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (D14) and 8.0% [5.5-9.9] after Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo (D70). The highest BDBV-reactive CD8response was observed in survivors (24.7% [20.3-33.1]), together with a prominent cytotoxic CD8 response (14.4% [10.4-19.7]) ; corresponding vaccine-group medians ranged from 0.9% to 17.7% and from 0.6% to 6.7%, respectively. SUDV responses were also detected, whereas MARV recognition was limited. BDBV-binding antibodies were detected following both vaccine regimens, with the highest levels observed in survivors (491 [330-1261] net MFI). Among vaccinees, EBOV- and BDBV-reactive cellular and humoral responses were positively correlated after adjustment for multiple testing. Interpretation EBOV infection and vaccination elicited BDBV-cross-reactive T-cell responses and binding antibodies. These findings support further evaluation of existing EBOV vaccines in the context of BDBV outbreaks. Funding INSERM, Vaccine Research Institute (ANR-10-LABX-77-01), and Institut de Recherche pour le Developpement (IRD).

items.title_en: Effect of protocolized MAGNesium replacement in critically ill patients On mortaLIty and Atrial fibrillation: protocol for the MAGNOLIA randomized controlled trial
items.abstract_en: Background: Measurement of serum magnesium levels, and administration of supplemental magnesium when levels are below target, is a common element of routine care for critically ill patients. However, targets for replacement vary, and the targets that lead to the best outcomes are unknown. Methods: Multi-center open-label parallel group randomized controlled superiority trial of adult critically ill patients receiving protocolized magnesium replacement, comparing a higher target (>0.95mmol/L) to a lower target (>0.7mmol/L). The trial will be embedded into the electronic health record (EHR) at 6 hospitals across 2 health networks in Ontario, Canada, with a shared EHR. We will include patients aged 16 years or older who have ICU admission orders, including an order for the magnesium replacement protocol. Patients with pre-eclampsia, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or neuromuscular junction disease will be excluded. Because both targets lie within the standard of care, we will use an opt-out consent approach. Screening will be integrated with the EHR, such that when a patient meets inclusion criteria, a pop-up will appear to allow the ordering clinician to confirm eligibility or indicate the relevant exclusion. After the clinician confirms eligibility, patients will be randomly assigned to a magnesium target. The primary outcome will be an ordinal composite, evaluated at 30 days, composed of death and the number of days free of atrial fibrillation or flutter in ICU. Secondary outcomes will include ventricular arrhythmia and antiarrhythmics administered; receipt of vasopressors, ventilation, and new renal replacement therapy in ICU; lengths of ICU and hospital stay; hospital mortality at 60 and 90 days, magnesium levels, and magnesium supplementation. For analyses, we will use Bayesian regression with weakly skeptical priors and an intention-to-treat approach. Outcome ascertainment will occur within the EHR. Discussion: This randomized controlled trial addresses an important uncertainty regarding routine care in the ICU with an EHR-embedded design. The innovative EHR-embedded design facilitates the large sample sizes and comprehensive, equitable recruitment needed for a trial evaluating a routine care intervention, and will lead to seamless integration with routine care upon trial completion. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07173855. Registered 12 September 2025, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07173855.

items.title_en: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
items.title_zh: 用于实时EEG相位估计的贝叶斯优化双二阶滤波器-Burg模型
items.abstract_en: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.

items.title_en: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
items.title_zh: iGC：基于学习到的体细胞超突变先验的强化学习抗体优化
items.abstract_en: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories. We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization. We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.

items.title_en: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
items.title_zh: 面向连续冷冻电镜异质性的经验贝叶斯流匹配
items.abstract_en: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures $x \in \mathbb{R}^{3N_a}$ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images $y$ generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior $p_θ(x)$ directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from $p_θ(x \mid y)$ via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.
items.abstract_zh: 本文研究从间接、含噪观测中学习高维隐变量生成先验的问题，聚焦冷冻电镜中的连续异质性：三维原子结构 x 无法直接观测，只能由复杂非线性前向算子生成的二维投影 y 推断。作者提出经验贝叶斯流匹配（EB-FM），在蒙特卡洛随机近似 EM 框架下直接从观测数据学习流匹配先验 p_θ(x)：E 步用引导式流生成从后验 p_θ(x|y) 近似采样，并以随机近似维持稳定的隐变量估计；M 步用这些隐变量更新流模型。该方法无需干净数据预训练，也能自然处理非线性前向模型。作者在 two-moons 与 MNIST 受控逆问题上验证，并在已知姿态的模拟冷冻电镜数据上表明，EB-FM 可在原子坐标空间直接恢复蛋白质构象的连续分布。
items.highlight_zh: 无需干净数据预训练，直接从投影图学出蛋白构象的连续分布
items.digest_zh:
「研究问题」冷冻电镜拍到的是大量二维投影图，而同一份蛋白样品中往往同时存在多种构象，即“连续异质性”。要从这些间接、带噪的投影反推三维构象的分布，是典型的“从观测中学习隐变量先验”的难题。
「方法」作者提出经验贝叶斯流匹配（EB-FM）。它把流匹配生成模型当作先验 p_θ(x)，用蒙特卡洛随机近似 EM 框架直接从观测数据学习：E 步通过引导式流生成从后验 p_θ(x|y) 近似采样，并用随机近似维护稳定的隐变量估计；M 步用这些隐变量作为训练目标更新流模型，两者交替进行。这样既不需要在干净结构上预训练，也能容纳复杂的非线性前向模型。
「结果」方法在 two-moons、MNIST 等受控逆问题上得到验证；在已知姿态的模拟冷冻电镜数据上，EB-FM 能在原子坐标空间直接恢复蛋白质构象的连续分布。
「意义」它把“无干净标签、非线性物理模型”下的贝叶斯推断与生成建模结合起来，为冷冻电镜连续异质性分析提供了一条免预训练的新路线。

items.title_en: Exploring the World of Lipids with Machine-Learned Coarse-Grained Models
items.title_zh: 利用机器学习粗粒化模型探索脂质世界
items.abstract_en: Lipid bilayers are central to cellular organization and function, yet their atomistic modelling remains constrained by its high computational cost. While coarse-grained (CG) models can overcome this bottleneck, they are limited in accuracy due to the use of simplified functional forms based on molecular mechanics. Using a hybrid functional form combining physics-based terms with a graph neural network, we present implicit-solvent, machine-learned CG models for POPC. When trained on single-lipid data, the model recovers the atomistic conformational landscape. By adding short atomistic simulations of a small flat bilayer to the training data and combining force matching with a denoising objective, we train a model that accurately reproduces bilayer structure and dynamics, in closer agreement with the atomistic reference than existing models, like Martini3 and DryMartini. Beyond its training data, the model stabilizes curved geometries, including vesicles, and captures complex cooperative phenomena such as bilayer and vesicle self-assembly and pore sealing. While limitations remain, particularly regarding chemical transferability, our results establish machine-learned coarse-grained potentials as a promising path towards robust and accurate CG models of lipids and membranes.

items.title_en: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
items.title_zh: 跨结构状态下蛋白质集合生成器设计选择的消融研究
items.abstract_en: Generative models of protein conformational ensembles inherit much of their design from structure prediction for folded proteins. Ordered and disordered proteins, however, occupy distinct structural regimes, and we investigate how design choices hold up across them. Using a minimal C$α$ flow-matching model, we ablate choices of architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment and training source, and evaluate each variant against experimental SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data partitioned into ordered, disordered, multi-domain and transitional proteins. Mixture-of-experts routing, a static pair representation and a disorder probe have no detectable effect, a smaller protein language model performs worse on ordered proteins but not on disordered ones, and alignment in the loss degrades agreement with SAXS. Replacing coarse-grained simulations of disordered proteins with fragment-assembled ensembles improves agreement with chemical shifts at a cost to SAXS, while an equal mixture of the two keeps most of the gain at a smaller cost. This points to the training data, rather than the architecture, as the main constraint.

items.title_en: Quantum Error Correction in Nearly Critical Toric Codes
items.title_zh: 近临界环面码中的量子纠错
items.abstract_en: We investigate quantum error correction protocols for topological codes deformed away from their stabilizer limits, particularly as they are pushed towards quantum phase transitions into trivial phases. Our focus is primarily on quantum information stored within the ground-state manifold of the transverse-field toric code (TFTC), subjected to independent bit-flip and phase-flip decoherence. Although the transverse field induces strong quantum fluctuations of $m$ anyons in the ground states, we show that projective measurements of the "bare" toric code stabilizers can nevertheless be used to construct an efficient decoding algorithm which exhibits a finite threshold to both types of decoherence, even when the transverse field is tuned infinitesimally close to the quantum critical point. Our construction of the optimal postmeasurement decoders---that is, the optimal decoders assuming that the stabilizers are first measured---crucially relies on the stoquastic nature of the TFTC Hamiltonian, which affords a description of its ground states in terms of a classical lattice gauge theory. Using stoquasticity, we first prove that stabilizer measurements act unitarily on the undecohered TFTC ground states to excellent approximation, and that the optimal postmeasurement decoder can be efficiently implemented via Monte Carlo simulation of a constrained lattice gauge theory. We then construct the optimal postmeasurement decoder for the TFTC states under bit-flip and phase-flip decoherence, where we numerically demonstrate a finite threshold close to the quantum critical point. We provide theoretical evidence (without a rigorous proof) that stabilizer measurements constitute an optimal decoding strategy in this setting. For phase-flip decoherence, we further prove that the optimal postmeasurement decoding threshold is independent of the transverse field strength throughout the topological phase.
items.abstract_zh: 本文研究拓扑码被推离稳定子极限、特别是被推向进入平凡相的量子相变点时的量子纠错方案，聚焦横场环面码（TFTC）基态流形中存储的量子信息在独立比特翻转与相位翻转退相干下的表现。尽管横场使基态中的 m 任意子强烈量子涨落，作者证明仍可用“裸”稳定子的投影测量构建高效解码算法：即使横场调到无限接近量子临界点，对两类退相干仍存在有限阈值。最优测量后解码器的构造关键依赖 TFTC 哈密顿量的 stoquastic 性质，由此可用经典格子规范理论描述基态，并能通过约束格子规范理论的蒙特卡洛模拟高效实现。数值结果显示临界点附近存在有限阈值，作者还给出理论证据（非严格证明）表明稳定子测量在此即为最优解码策略。
items.highlight_zh: 横场近临界环面码仍有有限纠错阈值，稳定子测量近乎最优
items.digest_zh:
「研究问题」拓扑量子纠错通常建立在稳定子形式（如环面码）之上。但真实器件或某些物态会被横场一类扰动推离这个理想极限，甚至逼近进入平凡相的量子相变点；此时任意子强烈涨落，“裸”的稳定子测量还算不算有效的纠错手段？
「方法」作者研究横场环面码（TFTC）基态流形中存储的量子信息，在独立的比特翻转与相位翻转退相干下的纠错。关键是利用 TFTC 哈密顿量的 stoquastic（矩阵元非正）性质，把基态写成经典格子规范理论，从而构造并分析“先测量、后解码”的最优解码器。
「结果」作者先证明稳定子测量在未退相干的 TFTC 基态上近似为幺正作用，最优测量后解码器可用约束格子规范理论的蒙特卡洛高效实现；随后构造出比特翻转与相位翻转退相干下的最优解码器，数值显示即使横场调到极接近量子临界点，仍存在有限的纠错阈值，并给出理论证据（非严格证明）表明稳定子测量就是该情形下的最优解码策略。
「意义」这说明拓扑纠错并不要求系统严格处于稳定子极限，在相变边缘仍可工作，拓宽了拓扑码在更真实条件下的适用范围。

items.title_en: Quantum Pointwise Dimension (QUPID): An algorithm for identifying classical chaos in quantum dynamics
items.title_zh: 量子逐点维度（QUPID）：一种识别量子动力学中经典混沌的算法
items.abstract_en: The Pointwise Dimension is a diagnostic that reveals the effective dimensionality of classical trajectories in a $2N$-dimensional phase space. The essence of this diagnostic is to find a scaling according to which density changes with radius $r$ around a point of interest in phase space. Particularly, regular trajectories are confined to an $N$-dimensional invariant torus, while chaotic trajectories explore a $(2N-1)$-dimensional energy surface. In classical mechanics, this trajectory density can be found by counting recurrences to within the sphere of radius $r$. In quantum mechanics, probability density is intrinsic, making the Pointwise Dimension compelling, but surprisingly this has not been studied in the quantum regime. In this work, we implement the Pointwise Dimension in the quantum regime using the Husimi representation of the quantum wavepacket. This implementation entails a long-time average of the time-dependent Husimi representation to obtain a stationary phase space density, and a radial spatial integration of this density over a sphere of radius $r$. The classical-quantum correspondence is excellent for both autonomous and non-autonomous systems, adding a new diagnostic to the study of quantum chaos. Finally, we explore the possibility, both classically and quantum mechanically, of obtaining the Pointwise Dimension from a time correlation function.
items.abstract_zh: 逐点维度（Pointwise Dimension）是一种诊断量，可揭示经典轨迹在2N维相空间中的有效维度：其核心是寻找一种标度关系，描述相空间中某点周围密度随半径r的变化。正则轨迹被限制在N维不变环面上，而混沌轨迹则遍历(2N-1)维能量面。经典力学中，轨迹密度可通过统计半径为r的球内回归次数得到。量子力学中概率密度是内禀的，因此逐点维度本应极具吸引力，但此前竟从未在量子情形下被研究。本文利用量子波包的Husimi表示，在量子框架下实现逐点维度：对含时Husimi表示作长时间平均以得到定态相空间密度，再对该密度在半径r的球内作径向空间积分。无论自治还是非自治系统，经典—量子对应都极好，从而为量子混沌研究增添了一种新诊断工具。最后，我们分别在经典与量子层面探讨了能否由时间关联函数获得逐点维度。
items.highlight_zh: 首次用Husimi表示把逐点维度推广到量子体系，识别量子混沌。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：如何判断一个量子系统的动力学是“类正则”还是“类混沌”？经典力学里有一个成熟工具——逐点维度：在相空间中某点周围取半径r的球，统计轨迹回到球内的频率，看这个密度如何随r缩放。正则轨道被束缚在N维环面上（N维相空间的一半维数），混沌轨道则铺满(2N-1)维能量面，二者缩放指数不同，于是维度就成了混沌的“指纹”。但量子力学没有确定的轨迹，只有内禀的概率密度，这一诊断此前从未被搬到量子层面。

方法：作者提出QUPID算法，用Husimi表示（一种把量子态映射成相空间准概率分布的工具）来承载波包。先对含时Husimi分布作长时间平均，得到不随时间变化的定态相空间密度；再以某点为中心，在半径r的球内对该密度作径向空间积分，拟合其随r的幂律标度，从而提取“量子逐点维度”。

结果：在自治与非自治两类系统上，量子算出的维度与经典结果高度吻合，说明经典—量子对应在这一诊断量上成立。作者还尝试用时间关联函数来间接获得逐点维度，为其实际测量提供可能路径。

为何重要：它给量子混沌研究补充了一个新的、可计算的诊断量，把经典相空间几何的直觉带入量子领域，并可能借助准概率分布实验测量，对量子—经典过渡研究有方法学价值。

items.title_en: Breaking the quantum barriers for Graph Collision
items.title_zh: 打破图碰撞问题的量子界限
items.abstract_en: In the graph collision problem, the task is to decide whether a known graph on $n$ vertices contains an edge with both endpoints marked, given query access to the input bits specifying the marked vertices. We first refute the conjectured $Ω(n^{2/3})$ query lower bound with a bounded error quantum algorithm using $\widetilde O(n^{92/139})$ queries. We then refine this approach to obtain a $\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ query algorithm. We also obtain a $\widetilde O((nq)^{11/17})$ query bound for all (partial) Boolean output functions with positive certificate complexity at most 2 and alphabet size $q$, contrasting a known $Ω(n^{2/3})$ lower bound for such problems with large alphabet sizes. We complement these algorithms with an $Ω(\sqrt{n\log n})$ quantum query lower bound for graph collision, exceeding the $O(\sqrt n)$ certificate complexity barrier for the positive adversary method.
items.abstract_zh: 在图碰撞问题中，给定一个已知的n顶点图以及查询被标记顶点比特的权限，任务是判断图中是否存在一条两个端点都被标记的边。我们首先用一个有界误差量子算法推翻了此前猜想的Ω(n^{2/3})查询下界，其查询复杂度为Õ(n^{92/139})。随后我们改进该方法，得到Õ(n^{11/17})查询的算法。我们还对正证书复杂度至多为2、字母表大小为q的所有（部分）布尔输出函数给出Õ((nq)^{11/17})查询上界，这与大字母表下已知的Ω(n^{2/3})下界形成对照。作为补充，我们证明了图碰撞问题的Ω(√(n log n))量子查询下界，突破了正对偶方法中O(√n)证书复杂度的障碍。
items.highlight_zh: 给出Õ(n^{11/17})量子算法，推翻图碰撞问题Ω(n^{2/3})的猜想下界。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：图碰撞（Graph Collision）是量子查询复杂度的经典基准问题。设有一个n个顶点的已知图，但每个顶点是否被“标记”要一位一位去查，问图中是否存在一条两端都被标记的边。此前人们猜想解决它至少需要约n^{2/3}次查询，这一猜想长期阻碍进展。

方法：作者构造新的有界误差量子算法。第一版算法用Õ(n^{92/139})次查询就打破了猜想下界，随后把技术提炼推广，得到Õ(n^{11/17})次查询的更强算法（注意11/17≈0.647，小于2/3≈0.667）。他们进一步把结果推广到一大类函数：凡正证书复杂度不超过2、字母表大小为q的（部分）布尔函数，都可用Õ((nq)^{11/17})次查询解决。

结果：上界方面，彻底推翻了Ω(n^{2/3})猜想；并指出在大字母表情形下已有Ω(n^{2/3})下界，因此新上界在q较大时依然有差距，揭示了字母表大小的影响。下界方面，作者证明图碰撞需要Ω(√(n log n))次查询，超越了正对偶方法（positive adversary method）通常止步于O(√n)证书复杂度的屏障。

为何重要：这项工作改写了量子查询复杂度中一个标志性问题的上下界地图，说明此前广泛相信的猜想可能是错的，也提供了能突破正对偶方法瓶颈的新下界技术，对量子算法理论有基础性意义。

items.title_en: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.title_zh: 读出“为什么”：光与量子比特上具有精确词证据的玻恩测量注意力
items.abstract_en: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 45% of test pairs, out of the 53% any single deletion can change, against 32% for the softmax model explained the same way and 40% by its attention x gradient. Attention can look more like the words annotators highlighted, yet accounts for the answer less well: deleting the word it ranks first changes the Born Transformer's answer in 32% of pairs. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and to qubits, and a coherent attention layer becomes one circuit equal to the model (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps by Hadamard tests, the device gave the model's answers on two short test pairs and kept or changed them under deletion as the model does; the evidence itself did not yet survive the device, and we work out the shots and calibration that measuring it on hardware would need.
items.abstract_zh: 当语言模型给出答案时，我们通常只能估计其原因。我们构建了一个每一步都是玻恩测量的Transformer：注意力为按行归一化的|⟨q|k⟩|^4，用测量式乘积替代前馈非线性，并采用玻恩读出。将分母固定为输入时的取值后，每个类别概率都是词振幅的多项式，因此其积分梯度证据可用有限求积精确计算、无求积误差：各词的贡献之和与类别概率超出无信息份额的部分一致，精度达10^{-11}或更好。在e-SNLI自然语言推理任务上，嵌入之外仅约98k参数，模型取得76.98±0.17%的测试准确率，与同规模softmax Transformer（76.62±0.36%）相当。删除其证据排名第一的词，会在45%的测试对上改变答案，而任何单次删除最多能改变53%；相同解释方式下softmax模型为32%，其注意力×梯度为40%。注意力可以更贴近标注者标出的词，却对答案的解释力更弱：删除玻恩Transformer注意力排名第一的词仅改变32%的答案。相同权重可精确编译为光电子光学系统与量子比特，一个相干注意力层成为与模型等价的电路（23个量子比特上852个CNOT门）。在IBM的ibm_kingston上，仅通过Hadamard测试读取注意力重叠，设备在两个短测试对上给出了模型答案，并在删除下按模型的方式保持或改变；证据本身尚未在设备上存活，我们分析了在硬件上测量它所需的采样次数与校准。
items.highlight_zh: 玻恩测量式Transformer使词级证据可精确计算，且能编译到光路与量子比特。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：大模型给出答案后，我们往往只能“估计”它为什么这么答——现有的归因方法（如梯度、注意力权重）都是近似的，且未必忠实反映模型的真实决策依据。能否设计一种模型，使“每个词贡献多少”可以被精确算出，而不是近似？

方法：作者把Transformer的每一步都改成量子力学式的玻恩测量：注意力用|⟨q|k⟩|^4并按行归一化；前馈非线性换成“测量式乘积”；输出用玻恩读出。关键技巧是把分母固定在输入时的数值，于是类别概率变成词振幅的多项式，其积分梯度证据可用有限求积精确求值，没有数值积分误差。

结果：在e-SNLI自然语言推理上，嵌入外仅约98k参数，测试准确率76.98±0.17%，与同尺寸softmax Transformer（76.62±0.36%）持平，说明改成玻恩形式几乎不损失性能。解释性上，删除证据排名第一的词可让45%的测试对改答案（单次删除上限为53%），远高于softmax模型同法解释的32%和注意力×梯度的40%；而单纯按注意力排序删除只改变32%，说明该模型的注意力反而“不如证据”忠实。此外，同一套权重可精确编译为光电子线路和量子电路（23量子比特、852个CNOT），并在IBM ibm_kingston上通过Hadamard测试读取注意力重叠，复现了两个短测试对的答案与删除行为，但完整证据尚未在硬件上存活，作者估算了所需采样与校准。

为何重要：它把“可解释”从近似事后归因变成模型内生的、可精确计算的量，并展示了向光子和量子硬件落地的可行路径，为可解释性与量子机器学习架起桥梁。

items.title_en: Interpretable Quantum Photonic Generative Models
items.title_zh: 可解释的量子光子生成模型
items.abstract_en: We propose a physical generative model for learning correlated multivariate data based on homodyne detection of photonic continuous-variable (CV) circuits. We use an $N$-mode photonic circuit in which two-mode squeezing provides correlations, local phase shifts tune the strength and sign of these correlations, and an adjustable interferometer redistributes them across modes. We train the circuit by matching its Pearson correlation matrix to the one obtained from data. We apply affine post-processing to adjust the marginals independently while keeping the relations intact. We test the model on the multivariate distribution of standardized log returns of financial assets, showing that the photonic model can represent rich correlation structures. We reproduce empirical correlations with residuals below $10^{-4}$ for five variables and recover the correct correlation signs for $94\% \pm 1\%$ of 190 correlation pairs at twenty variables, with $86\%$ of the residuals below $0.1$. As a separate technical contribution, we develop an approach for simulating Kerr gates with small nonlinearity via a Hubbard-Stratonovich expansion, making them suitable for CV-based simulators. Our results establish CV photonic circuits as a platform for interpretable generative learning, suitable for representing and fast sampling of distributions across different application domains.
items.abstract_zh: 我们提出一种基于光子连续变量（CV）电路零差探测的物理生成模型，用于学习具有相关性的多变量数据。所用N模光子电路中，双模压缩提供相关性，局域相移调节相关性的强度与符号，可调干涉仪将其重新分配到各模式。训练方式是令电路的Pearson相关矩阵匹配数据所得矩阵；再用仿射后处理独立调整各边缘分布而不破坏相关性。我们在标准化金融资产对数收益率的多变量分布上测试该模型，显示其能表示丰富的相关结构：五个变量时相关系数残差低于10^{-4}，二十个变量时在190个相关对中有94%±1%恢复出正确符号、86%的残差低于0.1。作为另一项技术贡献，我们提出用Hubbard-Stratonovich展开模拟小非线性Kerr门的方法，使其适用于基于CV的模拟器。结果确立了CV光子电路作为可解释生成学习平台的潜力。
items.highlight_zh: 光子连续变量电路可解释地学习多变量相关性，并用Hubbard-Stratonovich展开模拟Kerr门。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：生成模型通常像黑箱，学到的多变量数据中的相关性难以解读。作者想问：能否用物理上透明的光子电路直接“表示”数据中的相关结构，从而既快速采样又便于理解？

方法：构造一个N模连续变量（CV）光子电路。双模压缩产生模式间的相关性，局域相移调节每个相关性的强弱和正负号，可调干涉仪把相关性在各模式间重新分配。训练时不需要复杂的对抗或变分循环，只需让电路的Pearson相关矩阵去匹配从数据估计出的相关矩阵；各变量的边缘分布则用仿射后处理单独调整，保证不破坏已学到的相关关系。另有一项技术贡献：用Hubbard-Stratonovich展开来模拟非线性很弱的Kerr门，使其可在CV模拟器上实现。

结果：在标准化金融资产对数收益率数据上验证。5个变量时，重现的经验相关系数残差低于10^{-4}；20个变量、190个相关对时，94%±1%的相关对恢复了正确符号，86%的残差低于0.1。说明该电路能表达相当丰富的相关结构。

为何重要：该模型每个参数都对应明确的物理元件（压缩、相移、干涉），因此“可解释”：相关性来自哪里一目了然；同时光子硬件天然擅长快速采样，适合金融等需要大量模拟的领域。它把可解释生成学习与连续变量光子计算结合起来，并顺带解决了弱Kerr门难以模拟的工程问题。

items.title_en: Simple proof of conditions requiring maximal entanglement for local state verification and discrimination
items.title_zh: 局部态验证与区分中需要最大纠缠的条件的简单证明
items.abstract_en: For deterministic state verification by separable measurements, the Schmidt rank of an entangled resource must be at least that of the state being verified [N. Yu, R. Duan, and M. Ying, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 60, 2069 (2014)], and if the two are equal, the resource must be maximally entangled [S. Akibue, J. Miyazaki, and H. Osaka, Lett. Math. Phys. 116, 110 (2026)]. The latter was derived from a general theorem proved using algebraic geometry. In this paper, we give a simple, self-contained proof of both statements using only linear algebra. We then use these results to show that among pure entangled resources of local dimension at most $d$, a maximally entangled state of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$ is necessary and sufficient for perfect local discrimination of a generic orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$, however weakly entangled. The same holds for local implementation of a generic orthogonal measurement.

items.title_en: Effect of high odrer dispersion on soliton interaction in coupled Kerr cavities
items.title_zh: 高阶色散对耦合 Kerr 腔中孤子相互作用的影响
items.abstract_en: We investigate the interaction of dissipative Kerr solitons in two nearly identical coherently driven, coupled microresonators in the presence of third-order dispersion (TOD). Using an asymptotic reduction of the coupled Lugiato--Lefever equations, we derive effective interaction equations governing the soliton separation and collective drift for weak intercavity coupling. TOD breaks the parity symmetry of the soliton profile and qualitatively modifies the effective interaction, leading to asymmetric interaction forces and multiple stable and unstable soliton clusters. The existence and stability of these clusters are controlled by the relative phase of the driving fields and the group-velocity mismatch between the resonators. In particular, an appropriate value of the group-velocity mismatch can give rise to multiple stable bound states, whereas deviations from this value trigger successive saddle-node bifurcations, ultimately leading to periodic soliton collisions. The analytical predictions are confirmed by numerical simulations of the full coupled system.

items.title_en: Quantum Advantage has Few Complexity Implications
items.title_zh: 量子优势的复杂性意涵有限
items.abstract_en: We consider the complexity implications of proofs of quantumness and (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation. We show that both of these objects can coexist with the easiness of nondeterministic computation. That is, we give evidence that proofs of quantumness can exist when $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$ and that (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation can exist when $\mathsf{BQP} = \mathsf{QCMA}$. In particular, we give a classical oracle relative to which (1) $\mathsf{P}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{NP}^\mathcal{O}$ (2) $\mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{PSPACE}^\mathcal{O}$ (3) Proofs of quantumness exist. In particular, there exists a language in $\mathsf{IP}^\mathcal{O} \subseteq \mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O}$ which is hard on average against $\mathsf{P}^\mathcal{O}/poly$. We give a unitary oracle such that (1) $\mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{QCMA}^\mathcal{O}$ (2) Quantum verifier oblivious state preparation exists. These oracle separations directly imply a number of related consequences. For example, our first result implies that proofs of quantumness cannot be used to construct classical or quantum cryptography with a relativizing proof. Our second result implies that quantum computation/classical communication oblivious transfer cannot be used to construct post-quantum one-way functions with a relativizing proof.

items.title_en: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions
items.title_zh: 具有分数长程相互作用的量子相变的普适动力学
items.abstract_en: The complete statistical characterization of defects generated in a quantum phase transition has mostly been studied in exactly solvable models, and remains little explored in nonintegrable systems such as long-range interacting spin chains. We characterize the full defect counting statistics in a nonintegrable long-range spin chain, the fractional Ising model, by time-dependent variational-principle simulations within the matrix-product-state and matrix-product-operator formalism. Fractional interactions capture emergent multiscale correlations and long-range effects in nature, governed by the order of the underlying fractional derivative. Such couplings can be approximated on existing quantum simulation platforms, where the full defect statistics can be measured. The defect number cumulants follow power laws in the driving time, with exponents that vary continuously with the fractional order. At low fractional order, deep in the long-range regime, the mean defect number decays more slowly than predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), while at intermediate order the KZM holds with the numerically extracted many-body critical exponents. At large fractional order, the exactly solvable free-fermion limit of the model becomes progressively more accurate towards the short-range limit. We derive exact bounds on the kink-number cumulants and on the kink-kink correlations, implying an exact Gaussian limiting distribution for large system sizes. In the many-body simulations, however, kinks are more correlated, consistent with the confinement of domain walls, and these bounds are violated in the long-range regime, also in the bulk of the chain. Nevertheless, the kink distribution still approaches a Gaussian for large defect numbers, with proportionality partially broken between the cumulants.

items.title_en: Effective Hamiltonians and non-Hermitian physics
items.title_zh: 有效哈密顿量与非厄米物理
items.abstract_en: Every realistic quantum system is coupled to an environment. Including the environment restores a closed, Hermitian description, but at the cost of an intractably large Hilbert space. The Feshbach--Löwdin projection eliminates the unwanted degrees of freedom exactly, yielding an effective Hamiltonian $H_{\rm eff}$ on the relevant subspace alone---which \new{generically becomes non-Hermitian when the eliminated subspace contains an energetically accessible continuum and outgoing boundary conditions are imposed}. We illustrate this through a minimal model: a particle in a box with a delta barrier at its center. Direct elimination of one half-well reduces all information about the discarded sector to a single \new{boundary parameter} $β$; the same result is then rederived via the Green's function and Dyson equation, offering a pedagogical illustration of how boundary data enter the Green's-function formalism and relating $β$ to a self-energy term. Whether $β$ is real or complex determines whether $H_{\rm eff}$ is Hermitian or not, and the full range of behavior---from Hermitian dynamics through finite-width resonances to the counterintuitive quantum Zeno effect---follows from this single parameter.

items.title_en: DynaMite: Dynamic Measurement Scheduling To Accelerate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs
items.title_zh: DynaMite：加速容错量子程序的动态测量调度
items.abstract_en: Fault-tolerant quantum computers run millions of logical cycles to perform quantum error correction (QEC). As logical operations span entire logical cycles, the logical cycle time (LCT) dictates program runtime. Qubit measurements, critical to extract parity information for QEC, are the slowest operations and account for 43-86% of LCT. Measurement latencies impact fidelity: fast measurements lower our ability to correctly classify quantum states, whereas slow measurements increase the likelihood of decoherence. Hardware providers thus calibrate measurement latencies that maximize readout fidelity per qubit and use them to schedule all measurements during program execution. However, calibrated latencies are sub-optimal for logical performance because logical cycles span multiple QEC rounds, during which data qubits are not measured. This increases LCT and logical error rates (LERs) due to decoherence at the logical level. We propose DynaMite, a lightweight real-time measurement latency selection policy built on two key insights. First, logical cycles must use a measurement latency that is fast enough to reduce both LCT and LER for the QEC code, instead of the calibrated latency that only maximizes readout fidelity. Second, not all logical cycles are equal; many do not fully utilize the error budget of the QEC code, i.e., the number of failed parity checks it can tolerate without compromising LER. These cycles could use even faster measurements but do not, because latencies are chosen statically, whereas error information is only available at runtime. DynaMite exploits the fact that a logical cycle comprises multiple QEC rounds and selects the fastest latency for an upcoming round based on the error budget left and rounds remaining. Our evaluations show that DynaMite reduces LCT by 1.69x on average and up to 2.29x, and reduces LER to 0.46x on average and up to 0.13x of baseline.

items.title_en: Efficient simulations of spectra and transport for multiorbital quantum impurities
items.title_zh: 多轨道量子杂质的谱与输运高效模拟
items.abstract_en: Quantum impurity calculations become challenging when multiple correlated orbitals are treated explicitly, particularly in nonequilibrium steady states. We introduce Coupled-Cluster Coupled Lindblad (C$^3$L), a deterministic approach that combines the recently developed coupled-Lindblad compact bath representation with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions directly in imaginary and real frequency. C$^3$L has favorable polynomial computational complexity and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it agrees closely with state-of-the-art QMC while reducing computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude, with a further 10--100-fold speedup on a GPU. Beyond the practical reach of established real-time QMC solvers, four-orbital nonequilibrium impurities with general interactions and biased reservoirs become accessible with C$^3$L. We obtain resonance-resolved transport signatures relevant to scanning tunneling microscopy experiments on molecular junctions.

items.title_en: Analog signal processing, storage, and demultiplexing via in-materia wave-based computing
items.title_zh: 基于材料内波计算的模拟信号处理、存储与解复用
items.abstract_en: The ability of mechanical systems to perform basic computations has gained traction in recent years, providing a robust supplement to digital computing in off-grid, low-power, and extreme environments where electronics are inaccessible or risk failure. However, prior work has focused on Boolean logic applied via bistable structures, snap-through mechanisms, or origami lattices. Digital signal processing (DSP) underpins a wide range of computational tasks, providing the foundation for information encoding, manipulation, and analysis. In contrast to conventional DSP approaches, we present a new paradigm for analog information processing, where an elastic substrate houses a spatial wave-based platform for mechanical signal manipulation in the temporal domain. The proposed metasurface-based system exploits temperature-dependent phase transitions of shape memory alloys (SMAs) to realize key signal-processing functionalities, including gating, retention, and programmable delay of impinging mechanical loads. In doing so, we address a new set of challenges by manipulating transient mechanical waves through dispersive and lossy media. Building on this capability, we introduce the concept of mechanical wave-based memory, in which a locally resonant metamaterial's dispersion characteristics are actively reconfigured to achieve programmable delays while preserving spatial waveform integrity, and demonstrate its utility in the context of input shaping and frequency demultiplexing of superimposed waves. More broadly, the modular and scalable nature of the demonstrated framework paves the way for advanced mechanical computing architectures, enabling higher-order operations such as signal classification, parallel processing, and reservoir computing through the controlled sequencing and temporal alignment of mechanical signals.

items.title_en: Quantum Query Lower Bounds from Classical Moment Matching
items.title_zh: 基于经典矩匹配的量子查询下界
items.abstract_en: We prove a quantum analogue of the classical moment matching method, a popular framework used to prove lower bounds in property testing. For two random variables $X_0$ and $X_1$ whose moments match up to the first $r-1$ moments, the classical moment matching method says that no classical algorithm can reliably distinguish between input instances of length $N$ constructed from $X_0$ and $X_1$, respectively, unless it performs at least $Ω(N^{1-1/r})$ queries. While this method has been widely explored since its inception in the seminal work of Raskhodnikova, Ron, Shpilka, and Smith (STOC 2007) to prove lower bounds for symmetric properties, it has remained an open question whether a quantum analogue of it could be proved. We prove two variants of this quantum moment matching method, which are incomparable. Our first quantum query lower bound scales as $Ω(N^{1/2-1/(2r)})$, while our second moment matching theorem yields a sharper lower bound of $Ω(N^{1/2-1/(2(2^r-1))})$, albeit for smaller parameter ranges. Our results combine a new continuous hybrid argument with the polynomial method. The continuous hybrid argument compares two hard input distributions generated from i.i.d. samples by continuously varying both distributions, keeping them identically distributed at every intermediate stage. It reduces the comparison to the effect of changing the distribution of a single sample. The polynomial method then cancels the terms determined by the matched moments. We apply these moment matching theorems to prove new optimal lower bounds on $k$-distinctness, $k$-star-freeness, planarity and outerplanarity testing, as well as to improve prior lower bounds on image size testing and $K$-junta testing by logarithmic factors. A key advantage of our framework is its simplicity: it reduces quantum lower bound proofs to the construction of suitable moment-matching distributions.

items.title_en: Comment on "Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings"
items.title_zh: 对《基于量子哈密顿量嵌入的监督学习》的评论
items.abstract_en: We discuss the relationship between quantum Hamiltonian embeddings (arXiv:2610.26833) and prior developments in Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML), including QCML's earlier implementation on IBM quantum hardware. We consider the novelty claims and the computational role of encoding an entire dataset in a single ground state.

items.title_en: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits
items.title_zh: 变分量子电路的数据引导拟设选择
items.abstract_en: Choosing a variational quantum circuit (VQC) usually means searching over ansatze and depths, and training each candidate. We give three rules that fix these choices from the data and the gate set alone, before any training. First, a circuit without entangling gates has a rank-one Fourier coefficient tensor on every subset of qubits. A singular value decomposition of a dataset's Fourier coefficients therefore indicates whether entanglement is needed, which qubits it connects, and a lower bound on the error of omitting it. Second, the rank of the quantum Fisher information matrix grows by $p_0$ per layer, after a first-layer deficit $d_0$, until it reaches a ceiling set by the dynamical Lie algebra. This law fixes the depth. Third, reading out all $2^N - 1$ Pauli-Z products from one batch of shots resolves half of the state's directions, the most any single-basis readout can. A single-qubit readout resolves an exponentially small fraction. For the Madelon dataset, the rules prescribe 7 blocks of 3 qubits at depth 3: a 239-parameter classifier with 78.5% test accuracy, found without a grid search. Ablations confirm three predicted effects: shallower circuits, smaller blocks and dropping reuploading all lower accuracy.

items.title_en: Operational Thresholds for Long-Range Entanglement in Quantum Networks
items.title_zh: 量子网络中长程纠缠的操作阈值
items.abstract_en: Quantum networks distribute entanglement between distant nodes by combining many short entangled links using local quantum operations. These operations only succeed probabilistically, yet existing percolation-based theories of entanglement transmission treat them as perfect. We approach the problem through statistical physics, using a stochastic generalization of concurrence percolation to determine how reliable local operations must be for long-range entanglement to remain possible. On hierarchical $(U,V)$-flower networks, which permit full analytical control across network scales, we derive an exact renormalization recursion for the probability that an end-to-end entangled connection survives. For the $(2,2)$-flower this yields a closed-form operational phase boundary, $η_p = 2 - \frac{32}{27}η_s$, where $η_s$ and $η_p$ are the success probabilities of the series (entanglement swapping) and parallel (purification) operations, respectively. At this boundary the survival probability jumps discontinuously from $0$ to $S_\infty = 3/(4η_s)$. Numerically propagating the full distribution of end-to-end concurrence yields a second threshold in the initial link quality, which varies continuously with operational reliability. Above both thresholds the large-network state is binary: the connection either fails outright or approaches a perfect Bell pair. Our results thus reveal a two-threshold structure for long-range entanglement, in which operational reliability and initial link quality can compensate one another. Operational success rates therefore emerge alongside initial link quality as a primary design constraint for scalable quantum networks.

items.title_en: QECert: Formal Foundations for Quantum Error-Correction Theory in Lean
items.title_zh: QECert：Lean 中量子纠错理论的形式化基础
items.abstract_en: Quantum error correction provides the mathematical basis for protecting quantum information against noise. Existing formalizations have established foundations for stabilizer codes and code verification. However, a systematic formal treatment of the asymptotic constructions and fundamental limitations that underpin scalable quantum error correction is still needed. We present QECert, a Lean library providing reusable formal foundations for these theoretical questions. It connects quantum error-correction criteria, stabilizer and Calderbank-Shor-Steane codes, and algebraic and homological constructions within a common framework. Asymptotically good quantum low density parity check codes provide the principal case study. We formalize constructions and asymptotic parameter theorems spanning hypergraph products, balanced products, lifted products, and quantum Tanner codes. Further developments cover Bravyi-Poulin-Terhal bounds and related locality restrictions, constant overhead magic state distillation, and energy barriers and storage errors for quantum memories. QECert establishes a reusable formal foundation for studying the capabilities, resource requirements, and fundamental limitations of quantum error correction, supporting systematic verification and further development of its theory.

items.title_en: Reopening the one clean qubit case of a semi-grand challenge
items.title_zh: 重新探讨 semi-grand challenge 的单清洁量子比特情形
items.abstract_en: In his 2005 list of semi-grand challenges for quantum computing theory, Scott Aaronson asked whether a quantum computer that is always in a separable mixed state can be simulated by a classical computer in polynomial time. An affirmative answer was claimed for the one clean qubit model of quantum computation. The supporting mathematical arguments relied on an exhaustive characterization of circuits that stay in separable states. Here, we give a counterexample where one pure qubit, known as the clean qubit, controls a sequence of three gates that act on a maximally mixed three-qubit register. The overall unitary that accumulates as these gates are applied has the properties that ensure the state of all four qubits remains fully separable. Crucially, we show that the final unitary cannot be put into the form required by the claimed simulation result. We also give a continuous-time implementation of the same circuit that keeps the qubits fully separable throughout and ends at the same unitary. We extend our counterexamples to a uniform family, and pinpoint the gap in the earlier proof. Since our circuits are themselves efficient to simulate classically, this work does not settle Aaronson's question. It does, however, reopen the semi-grand challenge for an actively researched model of quantum computation.

items.title_en: Recoverability of Gravitational Entanglement under Decoherence
items.title_zh: 退相干下引力纠缠的可恢复性
items.abstract_en: Decoherence can make gravitationally generated entanglement arbitrarily small, or even vanishing, without necessarily rendering the effective matter dynamics separable. We ask whether this hidden non-separability can be revealed using strictly local quantum error correction. For Newtonian gravity supplemented by physically relevant localization noise, including environmental noise, and noise from collapse models such as GRW, CSL, and Diósi--Penrose, we analyze when the underlying entangling resource is locally recoverable. For GRW- and CSL-type noise, we analytically establish that strictly local quantum error correction can make the ratio of the effective gravitational interaction strength to the residual decoherence rate arbitrarily large for any parametrization of the collapse model, even in regimes where the unencoded entanglement signal approaches zero. By contrast, the Diósi--Penrose model does not exhibit the same enhancement under bipartite protocol considered here, revealing a qualitative difference. These results show that the loss of detectable entanglement is not equivalent to the loss of a recoverable non-separable resource, and open a route toward practical recovery protocols.

items.title_en: Ultracold polar molecules for quantum science and technology
items.abstract_en: Ultracold polar molecules present a rich platform for experimental quantum science leveraging their unique properties. Of particular relevance is the intrinsic electric dipole moment of the molecule, which results in strong coupling to microwave fields and can be used to engineer long-range, anisotropic, and tunable dipole-dipole interactions. Such interactions can generate entanglement between molecules and enable the study of novel quantum many-body phenomena in parameter regimes inaccessible in other systems. Modern experiments in optical tweezers and optical lattices have demonstrated controlled interactions between molecules in coherent quantum states, and recently bulk gases of molecules have been cooled to quantum degeneracy. Motivated by these landmark advances, we present this article to explain many of the key concepts relevant to current research in the field.

items.title_en: On Revolutionizing Power Systems: Suitability of Quantum Computing-Ready Pipelines for Stochastic Unit Commitment Optimization
items.abstract_en: Modern unit commitment (UC) scenarios, particularly those involving uncertainties from demand fluctuations and renewable energy sources, pose significant challenges to traditional optimization methods due to the large search spaces they encompass. This paper proposes a quantum computing-ready optimization pipeline for deterministic and stochastic UC, integrating classical, quantum-inspired, quantum annealing, and hybrid quantum-classical solvers across test systems, including the IEEE 118-bus system. A novel Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) reformulation accommodates generator scaling and 24-hour scheduling horizons with compact Boolean logic penalties for startup, cooldown, and spinning reserve constraints. A divide-and-conquer strategy and Quantum Computing Monte Carlo (QCMC) simulation address scalability across 27,730 uncertainty scenarios, reducing compilation time by up to two orders of magnitude. Experimental results demonstrate the pipeline's ability to achieve efficient, scalable, and accurate UC optimization under uncertainty: the hybrid quantum method approach matches the classical baseline, reduces stochastic UC runtime from 40.76 to 14.79 hours, and characterizes pure quantum annealing as limited to small systems with 0.22% to 2.18% encoding errors and constraint violations. These results provide an analysis of the scalability and computational practicality of hybrid quantum optimization for generator scheduling in UC.

items.title_en: ConvexAD: differentiable phase retrieval with geometric regularization for high-strain, low-signal Bragg coherent diffraction imaging
items.title_zh: ConvexAD：面向高应变、低信号布拉格相干衍射成像的几何正则化可微分相位检索
items.abstract_en: Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging (BCDI) relies on phase retrieval (PR), a non-convex, ill-posed inverse problem whose conditioning is degraded by factors like noise, partial coherence, and strain or crystallographic defects in the imaged nanocrystal. Conventional approaches, including alternating projections and deep learning methods, represent the object on a dense voxel grid, which is prone to amplitude-phase mixing and becomes increasingly ill-posed under these factors, often preventing reliable three-dimensional mapping of the particle's shape and strain. Here we present ConvexAD, a gradient descent PR model that parametrizes the object shape as a convex polyhedron, built by the intersection of half-spaces and enforces flat amplitude within it by construction. This geometric regularization eliminates amplitude-phase mixing and reduces the number of trainable parameters, hence facilitating the convergence of the PR. Implemented in JAX for native GPU acceleration and forward-model flexibility, ConvexAD is validated on simulated and experimental BCDI data, where it outperforms conventional and deep learning assisted PR at high strain, low signal, and reduced coherence, extending the conditions under which quantitative BCDI reconstruction is achievable.

items.title_en: Ergotropy Activation and Coherence in Dissipatively Charged Quantum Batteries
items.abstract_en: Quantum batteries can exploit quantum resources to enhance energy storage and work extraction, and recent experimental progress has brought their implementation closer to reality. In realistic settings, however, environmental dissipation is unavoidable, making dissipative charging a physically relevant operating regime. Here we investigate ergotropy in dissipatively charged quantum batteries, focusing on interaction-induced work extraction. For two coupled two-level systems (TLSs), we derive exact analytical expressions for the total, coherent, and incoherent ergotropy in both resonant and detuned configurations. We show that, in the resonant case, ergotropy is activated only above a critical coupling associated with an interaction-induced energy-level crossing, whereas detuning enables ergotropy already in the weak-coupling regime. Moreover, quantum coherence, although necessary for coherent work extraction, is not by itself sufficient to guarantee nonzero coherent ergotropy. In the strong-coupling regime, the resonant setup reaches the maximum ergotropy at a finite coupling strength, whereas the detuned setup approaches the same limit only asymptotically. Extending the analysis to a periodic XX spin chain of $N$ TLSs, we analytically derive the finite-temperature coupling threshold for ergotropy activation and show that it scales as $1/N$ in the large-$N$ limit. These results identify frequency detuning, interaction strength, and system size as key control parameters for ergotropy generation in open quantum batteries.

items.title_en: Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
items.abstract_en: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

items.title_en: Synchronization Mpemba Effect
items.abstract_en: We introduce the synchronization Mpemba effect, in which a less synchronized initial state overtakes a more synchronized one, and demonstrate it in dissipatively coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators. Within a graph-Laplacian framework, we show that for two oscillators, the mechanism is a competition between a slowly decaying collective background and a fast transverse transient, equivalently an exchange between relative-mode displacement and phase-fluctuation errors. The same decomposition extends to networks: the synchronization error splits into transverse Laplacian modes, yielding closed-form crossing times from eigenvalue separations and initial mode weights, and a sufficient screening criterion. With only these eigenvalues entering, the rule is topology independent: crossing times of different networks collapse onto a single spectral-gap line. Thus, quantum many-body dynamics can be designed and controlled at low dimension without constructing the exponentially large Liouvillian, opening a route to quantum synchronization as a resource.

items.title_en: Synchronization in one-dimensional arrays of photon condensates
items.abstract_en: We investigate the synchronization of coupled photonic Bose-Einstein condensates in dye-filled microcavity arrays, subject to a potential gradient. We show that in the absence of noise the desynchronisation threshold is the result of a dynamical instability. For a two-site system, we analytically derive the maximal potential difference that allows for a synchronized solution as a function of the system parameters and find that it crucially depends on the thermalization rate. For systems with $N$ sites, we find a $N^{-3}$ power law scaling for the critical potential difference. When quantum fluctuations are included, stochastic phase slips broaden the sharp transitions, yet the phase velocity and first order spatial coherence still reliably identify the instability threshold.

items.title_en: Band structure of two-dimensional graphene and of one-dimensional nanoribbons via variational quantum algorithms: from energies to wavefunction quality
items.title_zh: 通过变分量子算法研究二维石墨烯与一维纳米带的能带结构：从能量到波函数质量
items.abstract_en: Simulating quantum many-body systems classically encounters exponential bottlenecks, which quantum devices circumvent by natively encoding wavefunctions. In the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era, however, hardware noise constrains simulation accuracy. As a stepping stone toward strongly correlated materials, we compute the band structure of 2D monolayer graphene and 1D nanoribbons (zigzag and armchair) using a single variational workflow in the $p_z$ tight-binding approximation. Non-interacting ground states also provide essential initial reference states for subspace and warm-started variational methods to solve interacting spectra. By mapping the Bloch Hamiltonian to Pauli operators, we extract the ground band via the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and excited subbands via Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD), validating our approach from ideal simulations to execution on physical IBM Quantum processors. In ideal simulations, the workflow reproduces exact diagonalization results with high precision, whereas hardware noise introduces energy deviations of a few hundredths of the hopping parameter.
